A man has been jailed helping former soldier Daniel Khalife, who escaped prison and sparked a nation wide manhunt

Khalife escaped from HMP Wandsworth on the underside of a food delivery truck.

Adeel Khan, 32, from Waltham Forest, east London, helped his fellow inmate after his escape in 2023 by organising a way to get £400 cash to him.

Khan, who worked with Khalife in the prison kitchen, was convicted after trial in July this year and was sentenced at Snaresbrook Crown Court on Friday.

Another man, Imran Chowdhury, 26, of Chingford, east London, was cleared of the same charge of assisting Khalife after trial.

Khan asked Chowdhury to withdraw £400 for Khalife after his escape and arranged for him to be paid £120 for the job, the court heard.

open image in gallery Adeel Khan ( Met Police )

After his escape, Khalife called Khan multiple times using the phones of members of the public in a pattern of regular contact.

Khan messaged his then-girlfriend to pay Chowdhury who “didn’t know what was going on” for attending the meeting with Khalife.

At the time of the escape, Khan was on remand at HMP Wandsworth, facing extradition for France having been convicted in absence of playing a leading role in a human trafficking operation along with firearms offences.

He was described in court as the “leader” of a network organising trips for migrants from eastern Europe to France and then on to the UK via the channel. He was stopped while driving a van through France in 2021 and three boats, with engines and life jackets were found in the back, the court heard.

In sentencing, Judge Murray Shanks said: “These offences arose out of the escape from Wandsworth prison of Daniel Khalife on September 6 2023, at the time you were also in Wandsworth prison.

“You were remanded there awaiting extradition to France in relation to two very serious offences, or series of offences, for which you had already been sentenced in your absence.

“He [Khalife] was being held awaiting trial for a number of very serious offences under the Official Secrets Act and the Terrorism Act.

“In particular, he was working, it seems, with the Iranian secret service and giving details about members of the armed forces.”

open image in gallery Daniel Khalife at a branch of McDonald’s after he escaped from prison (Metropolitan Police/PA) ( PA Wire )

Khalife was sentenced to 14 years and three months in prison after being convicted of breaching the Official Secrets and Terrorism Acts at a trial in 2024.

Tom Williams, prosecuting, said: “Mr Khan’s assistance via Mr Chowdhury allowed Mr Khalife to buy the phone he used to contact his IRGC [Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corp] handlers.”

He added that Khan’s help meant Khalife was able “to survive on the outside for longer than he would otherwise have been able to” and that he used some of the money to buy non-prison clothes.

A red diary was found in Khalife’s possession when he was caught, which had Khan’s name, phone numbers and contact details for his relations, the court heard.

open image in gallery The truck used in the prison escape of Daniel Khalife, which was shown to the jury during his trial ( Metropolitan Police/PA Wire )

Khalife was also found with about £200 in cash which was thought to be part of the withdrawal Chowdhury had made.

Judge Shanks said: “He was only at large for a couple of days but he was assisted greatly, no doubt, by the money you organised from Wandsworth.

“By phone, first in receiving calls and then in making calls first to your girlfriend and then to your co-defendant.”

He later added that while Khan was not charged with assisting the escape itself, he was “quite sure” there had been some discussion about Khalife’s plan.

“That was why he had your number and your brother’s details I think when he escaped in that little book,” said Judge Shanks.

Gregory Fishwick, defending, told the judge that Khan looks after his family, many of whom were sat in court on Friday morning.

In July, Mr Fishwick told the court that Khan had “made decisions as a young man which he is now living to regret” including during his time in prison.

Khan, of east London, was sentenced to four-and-a-half years’ imprisonment for assisting an escaped prisoner and 15 months concurrently for his possession of an illegal prison phone.

News.title: Indonesia wildfires triggers 50,000 respiratory infections
News.content:
More than 50,000 people have contracted respiratory infections in Indonesia, as raging wild fires blanket huge swathes of the country in a thick, toxic smoke.

The vast archipelago is only a month into its fire season, but intense blazes have proven hard to control across Sumatra and Indonesian Borneo. There are fears the situation will only get worse, because the “Godzilla” El Niño is set to suppress rains that would normally have helped extinguish the flames.

“Our problems are not over. September is the peak of El Niño,” said Raja Juli Antoni, the forestry minister. “September is the main fight for us.”

Already the toxic haze has spread across Southeast Asia. On Friday Kuching, a city in Malaysian Borneo, was the most polluted city in the world on the IQ Air Index, followed by Jakarta and Singapore.

The wildfires have brought memories of record-breaking blazes in 2015. Then, the smoke was linked to roughly 100,000 excess deaths in Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore, according to one study. The World Bank said Indonesia alone saw economic losses of $16.1bn, or 2 per cent of GDP.

News.title: Global hunger is a threat to Britain’s national security, report says
News.content:
Global hunger poses a direct threat to Britain’s national security, and tackling it should be a government priority, a new report from the London School of Economics has warned.

It says hunger is a major driver of mass migration, extreme violence and war – events that threaten significant repercussions for Britain and Europe’s national security.

“Hunger prevention is an important part of national security policy, not an optional act of charity,” Stuart Gordon, professor of International Development at LSE and author of the report, told The Telegraph.

Recent hunger crises in places like Sudan, Afghanistan and across North Africa have contributed significantly to rising numbers of people moving to the West.

Between January and November 2025 alone, 12,684 migrants from Sudan – which is facing what has been described as the worst hunger crisis in Africa’s history – arrived in Europe, roughly three times as many as the previous year.

Last year, an estimated 155,000 African refugees arrived in Europe.

“Food insecurity tests one of the most basic expectations people have of government: that it will protect access to the essentials of life,” said Prof Gordon.

“Food price shocks can rapidly escalate into political instability when governments are perceived to have failed to protect access to basic subsistence goods,” he added.

News.title: Congo’s Ebola outbreak slows at epicentre but widens elsewhere, modelling suggests
News.content:
Congo’s Ebola outbreak shows signs of slowing at the epicentre of the flare-up, but is widening as the infection spreads further afield, modelling suggests.

The daily tally of new cases in Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) was falling at the end of August, but more cases were being found outside Ituri province, where the infection burst out.

Latest official figures say the outbreak has now killed more than 3,000 people out of over 6,100 confirmed cases, with the infection spreading faster than any previous epidemic of the viral haemorrhagic fever.

Modelling by Airfinity, a health analytics firm, suggests the true toll of cases could be more than four times higher than reported.

The outbreak remains on track to eclipse the 2014 West Africa outbreak later this month, to become the largest ever recorded.

Airfinity said that data from late August showed the seven-day averages of reported cases and reported deaths had fallen by 16 per cent and 18 per cent respectively.

The firm said it was “too early to confirm the decline will hold, and it may mask subnational variation: The outbreak has fluctuated before and a week of falling case and death counts does not rule out another surge.

“Even if the decline continues at this current pace, low case levels remain weeks away.”

News.title: Bank of England must raise interest rates, says chief economist
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. Government borrowing costs edged lower on Thursday as Andy Burnham continues to face scrutiny over the public finances.

The yield on 10-year US treasury bonds – considered a benchmark for what governments pay to borrow money – declined slightly to 4.78pc on Thursday after a drop in oil prices.

Pre-market trading of bonds in Britain, France and Germany suggested the market was poised to rally after a brutal first half of the week.

However, Mr Burnham and Chancellor John Healey remain under intense pressure, with analysts estimating that as much as half of the country’s fiscal headroom has been wiped out by the jump in bond yields.

Borrowing costs surged after a jump in oil prices caused by fresh strikes between the US and Iran.

The yield on 10-year gilts, as UK bonds are known, hit levels not seen since the global financial crisis in 2007, while longer-term debt costs hit their highest point since 1998.

It means the Chancellor will have less room for manoeuvre in the Budget next month, with some economists predicting the rise in borrowing costs has wiped out up to £14bn of breathing room.

The rise in bond yields across major economies had deepened concerns about deteriorating financial conditions.

Central banks in the US and Europe are increasingly expected to raise interest rates this month to combat inflation caused by the Iran war, although the Bank of England is expected to hold rates steady for now.

Gavin Friend, an analyst at NAB, said: “If this war ‌were to be ‌put to bed, then that ⁠would certainly be something very positive to bring yields back down again across the board.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

What happened overnight

Oil prices slipped, helping boost stocks and bonds.

Renewed fighting between the US and Iran pushed oil prices sharply higher earlier in the week.

However, Brent crude was trading near $94 a barrel after Donald Trump said he does not expect the US bombing campaign to last “much longer”.

Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 advanced 0.2pc to 64,455.83. Among major gainers, OpenAI investor SoftBank Group rose 2.9pc, memory chipmaker Kioxia rose 0.6pc, and chip equipment manufacturer Tokyo Electron gained 0.8pc.

South Korea’s Kospi rose 1.4pc to 6,656.81. Samsung was 1.3pc higher, while memory chipmaker SK Hynix was up 1.4pc.

In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng edged 0.1pc higher, to 25,344.80. The Shanghai Composite index climbed 0.4pc to 3,958.79.

Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 gained 0.5pc to 9,025.10.

The Taiex in Taiwan rose 0.6pc, while India’s Sensex climbed 0.3pc.

It comes after Wall Street bounced back after its sharp sell-off at the start of September, as investors snapped up shares that had fallen in recent days.

The S&P 500 rose, with almost 350 companies ending higher. Dell was among the biggest winners, jumping 14pc after giving an upbeat outlook, while investors were also looking ahead to results from chipmaker Broadcom.

The recovery came despite continued concerns over inflation, with oil prices remaining high as fighting between the US and Iran escalated. Brent crude briefly climbed close to $97 a barrel before easing back after Donald Trump said he did not expect the renewed bombing campaign to last “too long”.

US government bond yields were little changed after surging to their highest levels in several years earlier in the week.

Investors also got a mixed picture from the Federal Reserve’s latest assessment of the US economy. Economic activity increased modestly over the past two months, helped by strong demand from data centres, while companies added jobs at a slower pace in August.

The figures come ahead of Friday’s closely watched US jobs report, which could influence expectations for the next move in interest rates.

News.title: Weapons and mercenaries from foreign states fuelling Sudan’s war, UN report finds
News.content:
The war in Sudan is being fuelled by weapons and mercenaries from external states including the United Arab Emirates, Colombia and Turkey, a United Nations report has found.

An investigation by a UN fact-finding mission published on Thursday found that the supply of drones in particular to both sides in the civil war was extending the fighting’s reach and contributing to war crimes.

“Increasingly sophisticated drone capabilities [has] enabled both parties to strike far beyond immediate front lines”, says the report.

“The [UN] mission calls on States to enforce the Darfur arms embargo and suspend transfers of weapons, drones, components, or military assistance where there is a substantial risk of their use in serious violations”.

Sudan’s civil war erupted in April 2023 following a power struggle between the head of the military and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) as part of a planned transition to civilian rule. Hundreds of thousands have died and some 14 million people have been displaced in what has become the world’s deadliest conflict.

In a previous report in February, following the capture of El Fasher in which at least 60,000 people were killed, the UN said the RSF’s mass killings of Black African ethnic groups, including Zaghawa and Fur, bore the “hallmarks of genocide”.

The latest report said “individuals and entities” in the UAE were part of a transnational network supplying weapons, logistics, training and foreign personnel to the RSF – including NORINCO AH-4 howitzers, FK-20000 air defence systems and Chinese-made CH-95 strike drones.

The Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), meanwhile, separately obtained Turkish-manufactured drones, including Bayraktar Akıncı combat drones and Yiha III loitering munitions.

The Turkish embassy in London has been contacted for comment.

News.title: The Ukrainian children struggling to survive alone in Europe
News.content:
Every day begins and ends in the same way for Arsenii, 17: calling his mum back home in Kyiv. A year ago he moved from Ukraine to a school boarding house in Slovakia. One night he fell asleep before phoning. When he woke, his mobile was flooded with messages from the few adults his mum knew in the country: the dorm security guard and agent she paid to become his temporary legal guardian. “She woke up everybody,” he says, still with a sense of guilt. She had been trying, agonisingly, to account for her son from over 1,000km away.

Russia’s unprovoked full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 triggered Europe’s largest displacement of children since World War II. More than 1.8 million crossed into neighbouring countries in the first month – 90 per cent of them with their mothers or other female relatives. But as bombardments battered the country in the following four years, children continued to leave – only without their relatives.

A year-long investigation by the Telegraph has discovered thousands of Ukrainian children are living in Europe alone in the hope of a better life. Some have adapted to independent living, studying and learning the local language. Others have fallen into illegal work, experienced insecurity and discrimination. A few attempts end in tragedy.

The exact number of Ukrainian children who are now living alone in Europe is unclear. Data collected by EU statistical database Eurostat suggests the total cases since 2022 could be almost 23,500. It shows that 19,580 unaccompanied Ukrainian minors in European Union (EU) countries received EU Temporary Protection Status (TPS) between March 2022 and July 2026.

Non-EU countries offer parallel protection schemes. Eurostat data revealed that in the same time-frame, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland granted their protection status to an additional 3,905 unaccompanied Ukrainian minors.

However, the data is incomplete. Only 20 out of 27 EU members declared their numbers. Among those missing are key Ukrainian refugee destination countries, such as Germany and Poland. Poland alone issued 42,332 temporary guardian orders to Ukrainian minors between 2022 and 2025, according to Polish Ministry of Justice data requested by The Telegraph.

In theory, any child granted TPS protection should have a locally appointed legal guardian to sign their papers. However, our investigation revealed loopholes in the system, leaving this category of children vulnerable to abandonment or poor guardianship arrangements.

Arsenii is among at least 1,024 Ukrainian children aged 14 to 16 who have evacuated to Slovak school boarding houses, according to a snapshot 2025 survey by the Slovak Children’s Commissioner. The real figure is likely to be thousands higher, as this research covered just over half of secondary schools in five of the country’s eight regions. It concluded some 5,000 Ukrainian minors in Slovakia have no responsible adult “close to them”, of whom around 1,000 have no legal representative at all.

News.title: Zika virus mosquitoes breed in Britain for first time
News.content:
The UK has historically been too cold for the tropical mosquitoes to survive, but they have been slowly making their way up through Europe.

As temperatures warm, it is predicted that the mosquitoes could become widespread, potentially bringing with them diseases associated with Africa and the tropics.

“The timing of this detection is particularly interesting because the UK has just experienced its provisionally hottest summer on record,” Dr César López-Camacho, a researcher at the University of Oxford, said.



“Warmer conditions can accelerate mosquito development, extend the period in which mosquitoes remain active and, critically, increase the rate at which viruses such as dengue or chikungunya replicate within a competent mosquito,” Dr López-Camacho added.

Previous government modelling suggested that the mosquitoes would be unlikely to get a foothold in Britain until 2040, but the new discovery of the colony in London suggests it may happen sooner.

It means diseases such as dengue fever – which causes high fevers and severe joint pain, and can be fatal, particularly in the elderly and young children – could become common in southern England.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford gets new Man Utd tattoo on Old Trafford return after 18 months away
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford gets new Man Utd tattoo on Old Trafford return after 18 months away

Marcus Rashford is back in the fold at Manchester United after being frozen out by Ruben Amorim and now looks set to play a key role under Michael Carrick this season

View 4 Images Marcus Rashford is back in the Manchester United fold (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Marcus Rashford has a new tattoo to represent his new shirt number after being reintegrated back into the Manchester United team.

‌



The England attacker, 28, looked to be on his way out of Old Trafford for good last summer after joining Barcelona on a loan deal with an option to make the move permanent. And even after the Spanish giants deciding against triggering said option, Rashford has continued to be linked with a move away.

‌



But with Michael Carrick now at the helm, Rashford is back in the fold at The Theatre of Dreams and started in the emphatic 5-2 win over Ipswich Town last Sunday.

‌



Rashford has been given the No.9 for the new campaign, which most have taken as another pretty strong indication that he has been earmarked to play a significant role under Carrick.

And the boyhood United fan has added the iconic shirt number to his tattoo collection of previous shorts worn.

‌



Rashford's previous shirt numbers are already tattooed on his body. In a new social media update, Rashford has added both the No.9 and the No.14 shirt he donned while on loan at Barcelona last season.

His return to the first-team fold at Manchester United comes 18 months after his career at the club was effectively over.

4 View 4 Images 4 View 4 Images

‌



Rashford was first loaned out to Aston Villa after being frozen out by Ruben Amorim, followed by his move to Barcelona last summer.

Speaking after the attacker impressed in his favoured left wing spot against Ipswich, Carrick declared that having Rashford back in the fold was essentially like another new signing.

"I think the situation that we're in, I think the business that we've managed to do, I'm pleased with, he said. "I think we're a better group, a better squad, potentially a better team. Adding Marcus (Rashford) into that feels like a new signing. So, in that respect, we're quite happy."

‌



View 4 Images Rashford started in United's thumping 5-2 win over Ipswich Town

Carrick added: "[I'm] really pleased with Marcus. He's adding to the group for us, for sure. He's one of our own. He's living his dream, playing here now and trying to be successful and win.

"So, whatever's gone on, I think part of this club, there are players that have come and come back sometimes, or players that maybe were going to leave, didn't leave.

Article continues below

"It's always about what you do next and what your intentions are. He's been fantastic since he came back, I have to say."

Sports.title: 'I made my Man Utd debut with Marcus Rashford – now I have new career selling insurance'
Sports.content:
'I made my Man Utd debut with Marcus Rashford – now I have new career selling insurance'

An ex-Manchester United player now lives a very different life

View 3 Images Former Manchester United talent Joe Riley now sells insurance (Image: Getty)

A former Manchester United prospect who made his debut alongside Marcus Rashford now sells insurance for a living. Joe Riley started at left-back under Louis van Gaal 10 years ago against Danish side Midtjylland in the Europa League.

‌



The then-19-year-old played 79 minutes and received an Old Trafford standing ovation when he was eventually subbed off on his debut. As it so happened, Rashford also made his first start for the club in that same fixture.

‌



However, the former Red Devils team-mates’ careers have panned out very differently over the past decade. Rashford, since his incredible two goals in that game, has gone on to make more than 400 professional appearances at the top level, along with 78 England caps.

‌



The 28-year-old has scored 156 goals for United, Aston Villa and Barcelona, while representing his nation at three World Cups. But Riley, who played in the Under-18s alongside Rashford, Napoli’s Scott McTominay and Crystal Palace’s Dean Henderson, now balances semi-professional football with an entirely different career.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd, Arsenal and Liverpool name Champions League squads as Reds snub two senior stars READ MORE :

Riley told BBC Sport: "I lived with Scott McTominay for six years, and Marcus and I also came through the academy together. These people were like family to me.

‌



"Of course I would have liked to have played more games for United but things didn't work out like that. I don't dwell on the past - I'm just happy that it happened.

"I've now got my foot in the door for the next chapter of my life. I'm progressing with another career that's setting me up for the rest of my life."

View 3 Images Riley and Rashford made their United debut in the same game (Image: Getty )

‌



Rashford went on to play several more times that season, including United's FA Cup final win over Crystal Palace at Wembley. Riley did not appear again for the senior side. He continued to train with the first team after Van Gaal was sacked and replaced by Jose Mourinho in May 2016, and was named captain of the under-23s. By 2017, however, injuries were starting to disrupt his career.

Riley left United at the age of 21 with just two first-team appearances under his belt before dropping down the leagues, having suffered bad luck with injuries. It was during one of those niggles that he decided to start studying for a new career.

The full-back, who grew up in Lytham, Lancashire and joined United aged six, now plays for Warrington Rylands in the seventh tier of English football. The Northern Premier League Premier Division side face Hyde United in the first qualifying round of the FA Cup on Saturday.

‌



View 3 Images Riley quit professional football to take on a different career (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

Now 29, Riley works for a company in Sale, near Manchester, after ending his full-time playing career following spells in the National League with Fylde and Tamworth. He sells life insurance, income protection, critical illness and injury cover as a financial protection advisor alongside his non-league career.

"I'm loving it," Riley said. "Moving from full-time football to part-time was something I once feared, like many players do. Instead my job is rewarding, while I joined Warrington Rylands in the summer - a club I thoroughly enjoy being at.

Article continues below

"I've started my exams to become a wealth manager to help with investments and pensions. I don't want to play full-time again. Even if an opportunity arose, I'm too far down the road in terms of preparing for life away from football."

Sports.title: 'I cried when Man Utd transfer fell through – I wanted to stay at Real Madrid'
Sports.content:
'I cried when Man Utd transfer fell through – I wanted to stay at Real Madrid'

Manchester United are a dream destination for many players, though one target disclosed how relieved he was a transfer to Old Trafford collapsed at the 11th hour

View 2 Images Keylor Navas once spoke of his relief that a move to Manchester United from Real Madrid collapsed (Image: Angel Martinez/Real Madrid via Getty Images)

Former Real Madrid goalkeeper Keylor Navas once described his relief that he would not be joining Manchester United. So happy was he to miss out on a move to Old Trafford that he cried when the move was ruled out.

‌



The Costa Rica legend was heavily linked a move to United at several points in his career. The transfer looked most plausible in the summer of 2015 after a fairly unremarkable debut season at the Bernabeu.

‌



Navas, 39, was close to trading places with ex-United stopper David de Gea before the infamous deadline-day fax incident saw the move fall apart. Most players might be sad to miss out on joining United, but the very opposite was true for Navas.

‌



"I cried that night when I found out I was staying, it was a build-up of emotions," he said during a 2015 interview with radio station Cadena COPE. "I didn't want to leave, Madrid is my home.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"I never wanted to leave Real Madrid. My agent told me to be alert to my phone. We had to go to Barajas [airport], although I never actually got on a plane - I was in a waiting room. I thought that if God wanted me to leave Madrid, it would be for the best, but he didn't want me to..."

‌



Navas and De Gea looked all set to trade clubs in 2015, with United also due to receive £29million as part of the part-exchange deal. However, a fax malfunction was blamed for the deal collapsing after United submitted the paperwork two minutes past the midnight deadline.

‌



De Gea, on the other hand, remained at United during what was a disappointing period in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson years. An era of general decline at Old Trafford made the goalkeeper job at United an unenviable position as the club's title prospects fell through the floor compared to past iterations.

Now playing at Pumas UNAM in Mexico's Liga MX, the veteran talent continues to impress as his fourth decade comes to a close. He went on to win a catalogue of domestic titles over the course of five years in Paris before departing in 2025.

Sports.content:
7 players Man Utd could sign in 2027 including defensive overhaul and dream left-back

Manchester United may have closed the summer transfer window, but the club are already eyeing potential targets for January and beyond

View 8 Images Michael Carrick will be looking to the January transfer window (Image: Dan Mullan, Getty Images)

The summer transfer window may have shut, but the wheels at Manchester United never stop turning. With Michael Carrick having overseen a flurry of incomings at Old Trafford, the United boss is already thought to be plotting his next moves as the January window edges closer and the blueprint for next summer begins to take shape.

‌



Carrick's recruitment team did not stand idle this summer, bringing in Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba to bolster the engine room.

‌



Goalkeeper Karl Darlow also made his way to Old Trafford on a free transfer following his departure from Leeds United. Tynan Thompson, Kit Margetson and Cristian Orozco also completed moves to the club.

‌



Yet for all the activity, certain areas of the squad remain a source of concern. Defensive depth, positional cover and further quality in midfield are among the priorities yet to be fully addressed. Here, we run the rule over the seven names most likely to be in consideration for United.

Alex Scott

Chelsea were unsuccessful in their attempts to lure Bournemouth midfielder Scott to west London this summer, despite tabling a £64m bid.

Mike Dean sparks outrage as ex-Premier League ref admits to secret games during matches READ MORE :

Fenerbahce issue Mason Greenwood statement as UEFA investigate ex-Man Utd star READ MORE :

The 23-year-old's deal with the Cherries runs until the summer of 2028, with United equally keen on the gifted star as they seek to strengthen their central midfield.

‌



View 8 Images Alex Scott was of interest to a number of clubs this summer (Image: Mark Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Scott even declined to put pen to paper on a fresh contract this summer, meaning United could land the player at a reduced cost next year as he enters the final 12 months of his time on the south coast. The fact that Scott's step-sister Maya Le Tissier also captains United's Women's side could further tempt him towards a switch to Old Trafford.

Aurelien Tchouameni

United have held a longstanding admiration for the Real Madrid midfielder, stretching back to his days at Monaco, and once again he was strongly tipped for a move to Old Trafford this year. The French international's contract at the Bernabeu is set to expire in the summer of 2028.

‌



View 8 Images Aurelien Tchouameni has been linked with a move away from Real Madrid (Image: Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

It might be something of an outside bet, with Madrid undoubtedly looking to command a substantial fee for the 26-year-old World Cup winner. Yet the reality is that next summer could represent the perfect conditions for United to finally make their move for the world-class defensive midfielder.

Should he find himself short of game time at Real Madrid this season, following the La Liga giants' flirtation with the idea of offloading him over the summer, Tchouameni could potentially become an attractive proposition on the market in twelve months' time.

‌

Micky van de Ven

The club were linked with a move for Micky van de Ven this summer, only for the Dutch defender to put pen to paper on a fresh deal. He was also handed the captaincy at Spurs, making any renewed approach considerably more difficult.

View 8 Images Micky van de Ven signed a new deal with Spurs this summer (Image: News Images/NurPhoto)

‌



However, should Lisandro Martinez's injury troubles persist, Van de Ven appears an obvious target for United boss Carrick. While it remains a long shot, the club are expected to sound out their options for the pacey 25-year-old if Tottenham's struggles on the pitch continue.

Jarrad Branthwaite

United's pursuit of Premier League-proven talent could see them return to Everton's Branthwaite. The club have previously lodged a bid for the Toffees defender.

View 8 Images Jarrad Branthwaite of Everton (Image: Gary Oakley/Everton FC/SmartFrame)

‌



The centre-back, who can also fill in at left-back, agreed personal terms over a switch to Old Trafford, only for Everton to turn down two bids from United in the summer of 2024. Branthwaite has been hampered by injuries since, but at just 24, the commanding defender still has plenty to offer.

Lewis Hall

With United left relying on Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui as the only senior options to deputise for Luke Shaw, alongside 19-year-old Harry Amass, left-back has emerged as the most pressing position to strengthen.

View 8 Images Lewis Hall continues to be linked with Man United (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Hall emerged as United's dream option for the position this summer, but it quickly became apparent that Newcastle had no intention of selling following an exodus of high-profile players. Nevertheless, the 21-year-old was keen on the move to Old Trafford, and United are widely expected to reignite their pursuit of Hall next summer.

Alejandro Balde

United were thought to have had their eye on the Barcelona left-back this summer, but pulled out of a potential deal due to a disagreement over the defender's valuation.

View 8 Images Alejandro Balde could solve Manchester United's left-back issue (Image: Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



Still just 22, his contract with the Catalan club runs until the summer of 2028. Barcelona's acquisition of Joao Cancelo, combined with the emergence of Xavi Espart, is only likely to further tempt United into returning with an offer for Balde.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Cody Gakpo's future clear as star issues statement after late transfer drama
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Cody Gakpo's future clear as star issues statement after late transfer drama

The fallout from a chaotic deadline day in the transfer window continues for Liverpool

View 2 Images Cody Gakpo almost left Liverpool this summer (Image: 2025 Getty Images)

On Friday evening, Andoni Iraola will lead his Liverpool side into a Premier League game without the buzz of the transfer window hanging over him for the first time this season. Liverpool are looking for their first win of the new campaign, having drawn their opening two fixtures against Newcastle United and Nottingham Forest.

‌



Premier League new boys Ipswich Town, at Portman Road, are the challengers. While many fans will be eager to put transfers behind them for now and turn their attention to on-pitch matters, the fallout from the Reds' summer window continues regardless.

‌



One of the primary talking points over the last few months has been Cody Gakpo's proposed departure, with Tottenham and Manchester City registering their interest in the player. Another was the host of players leaving Anfield as the window sped to a conclusion.

‌



Today's news sees Iraola address Gakpo's current feelings after his cancelled transfer, while a departing star has made his thoughts clear on his Anfield exit.

Gakpo's future clear

Cody Gakpo appears undeterred and ready to go despite almost leaving Liverpool on deadline day. After being courted by Tottenham Hotspur for much of the summer, the Dutchman became a target for City, who were willing to pay around £85million for the 27-year-old forward.

Mo Salah jets back to Liverpool as wife gives birth to third child with name revealed READ MORE :

Andoni Iraola gives update on Bradley Barcola and when he could make Liverpool debut READ MORE :

The switch would only have materialised if Liverpool had brought in another attacker. But with moves for Crystal Palace's Isamaila Sarr and Brighton's Yankuna Minteh not forthcoming, Gakpo's exit was blocked as the Reds rejected City's bid.

‌



The Dutch star, who has started the season well, will be in the squad to face Ipswich. Iraola has claimed he has had an open dialogue with Gakpo throughout the transfer drama and is happy to pick him for the Premier League tie.

View 2 Images Cody Gakpo has a goal and an assist from the opening two games of the season (Image: Getty Images)

"My relationship with Cody has been very honest from the beginning," The Basque head coach said. "He has played very well for us so far. He was always aware of the situation in the market, we were constantly talking, I hope we can keep him at the same level. He is in a good place physically and mentally and I'm very happy to pick him."

‌

Stefan Bajcetic has released a heartfelt message on social media as his time at Liverpool came to an end. The midfielder completed a transfer to Celta Vigo on August 31.

Liverpool signed Bajcetic in 2021 and he broke into the first team a year later and looked set to star in the midfield for years to come. However, a calf injury wrecked his development and forced him to miss most of the 2023/24 season. The 21‑year‑old then struggled in loan spells at Red Bull Salzburg and Las Palmas.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Having entered the final year of his contract at Anfield, Liverpool decided to sell Bajcetic for a profit rather than risk losing him for nothing next summer. The midfielder has no hard feelings, clearly.

Part of the Spanish star's message read: "The love you have gave me throughout the 5 years I spent in Liverpool has been incredible, it’s easy to show love when things go in the right direction, but as you know it hasn’t always been the case with me, and you have been there for me at all times.

‌



"This club is a massive family and it wouldn’t be with all the people that work for it, from chefs, kitchen staff, player care, groundskeepers, media, kit man, and all the hundred departments this club has, everyone makes out life so much easier and keeps this club as big as it is. I will miss you so much.

"Physios, doctors, medical department, what can I say, unfortunately, we got to spend so much time together, we lived so many ups and downs, and you have always gave your best for me, I will always be grateful. This club will stay in my heart forever. Once a red, forever a red."

Sports.title: Arsenal could sign Barcelona star, wonderkid striker and free agent in transfers next year
Sports.content:
Arsenal could sign Barcelona star, wonderkid striker and free agent in transfers next year

Mikel Arteta could make some major additions to his Arsenal squad from as early as January

View 6 Images Mikel Arteta has some decisions to make (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Arsenal could improve their squad even further in just a few months after spending almost £200million this summer. Mikel Arteta added more firepower to his midfield and defence by securing Bruno Guimaraes, Ezri Konsa and Piero Hincapie.

‌



Christos Tzolis was the only attacking signing made by the Gunners after he joined from Club Brugge. Arteta had urged the club to "make some very important decisions" during the window but they failed to secure a marquee forward addition.

‌



Arsenal did make attempts for Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez and Vinicius Jr from Real Madrid but they failed to materialise. The club also sold Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and allowed Gabriel Martinelli to depart for Al-Hilal in a deal worth £60m.

‌



Viktor Gyokeres, Kai Havertz, Max Dowman, Noni Madueke, Eberechi Eze and Bukayo Saka are still on the Gunners' books this season. But if the club struggles in attack in the near future, then Arteta could make some exciting moves to add to his squad.

Arsenal medical underway with third Gunners signing already lined up for 2027 READ MORE :

Here, Mirror Football have looked at five players Arsenal could sign in the next couple of windows.

Julian Alvarez

The transfer saga concluded with Alvarez staying put at Atletico Madrid. Despite the Argentina international reportedly favouring a switch to Barcelona, the forward's decision could shift over the coming months.

‌



View 6 Images Arsenal did move for Julian Alvarez (Image: Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Should Arsenal manage to secure Alvarez, the 26-year-old could be a major coup for the club's attack.

Eli Junior Kroupi

Bournemouth were resolute that Kroupi would not be departing this summer, and their position was strengthened by the 20-year-old's recovery from injury. The gifted forward drew widespread interest after scoring 13 league goals for the Cherries last season and Arsenal reportedly maintained an interest in Kroupi prior to the summer transfer window.

‌



View 6 Images The Gunners were also keen on Eli Junior Kroupi (Image: Robin Jones - AFC Bournemouth/AFC Bournemouth via Getty Images)

The Independent reports that Kroupi will "almost certainly" be an option the Gunners revisit in January. Signing him would substantially strengthen Arteta's choices, both immediately and for the future, with Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres vying to be the club's leading striker.

Andreas Schjelderup

Should Arsenal be willing to wait until next summer for a new left-winger, Benfica star Andreas Schjelderup could turn out to be a steal. New signing Tzolis will only have Eze for competition on the left flank after the Gunners decided to cash in on multiple forwards this summer.

‌



View 6 Images Andreas Schjelderup has bags of potential (Image: Maciej Rogowski/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images)

Schjelderup's contract runs until 2028, meaning the Norway international will enter the final 12 months of his deal next summer, potentially resulting in a reduced transfer fee. The 22-year-old is a promising talent with considerable scope for development.

Raphinha

A left-winger who would provide Arsenal with an immediate solution out wide. The 29-year-old is the Barcelona captain but will be in the final year of his contract next summer.

‌



View 6 Images Raphinha could be convinced to return to England (Image: Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

The Brazilian boasts extraordinary talent, having netted 80 goals and laid on 60 assists in 180 appearances for the Catalan club. Bringing Raphinha to the Emirates would also allow Arsenal to harness his wealth of experience and winning mentality.

Karou Mitoma

Arsenal could replicate their Leandro Trossard masterstroke by swooping for Karou Mitoma as an established Premier League performer from Brighton.

‌



View 6 Images Kaoru Mitoma would be a smart signing (Image: Sebastian Frej/MB Media/Getty Images)

While not a long-term solution, the 29-year-old is entering the final year of his contract and could thrive within Arsenal's setup, either as a cut-price January signing or on a free transfer next summer.

Sports.title: Gasly loses Monaco GP podium again after McLaren, Red Bull win appeal
Sports.content:
Alpine's Pierre Gasly has lost his third-place finish from June's Monaco Grand Prix again after his penalties from the race were reinstated after a successful appeal by McLaren and Red Bull.

It means Red Bull's Isack Hadjar reclaims third place with McLaren's Oscar Piastri back into fourth.

Gasly is reclassified in seventh place with Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad fifth and sixth respectively.

The June 7 race was won by Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton second.

Gasly finished third on the road but was originally classified in seventh after two unserved five-second time penalties for pit-lane speeding were applied immediately after the chequered flag.

Alpine won a right of review case five days later after presenting new evidence to stewards showing Gasly had not, in fact, been speeding, which at that point saw the penalties annulled.

Sports.title: The assistant headteacher about to become England manager for a week
Sports.content:
Andy McCann has only just returned to work.

By day, he works as an assistant headteacher at Great Sankey High School in Warrington. The summer holidays have come to a conclusion and the school year is back in full swing.

But he is about to take eight days off in order to become England manager... sort of.

That's because McCann is also the manager of the Cheshire League, a representative team made up of the best players from the Cheshire League Premier Division.

His side won the FA Inter-League Cup by beating the Herts Senior County League at Leicester's King Power Stadium on May 9 - and, in doing so, earned the chance to represent England in the UEFA Regions Cup.

So, first things first, what is the Regions Cup?

It is an amateur tournament founded in 1996 and held every two years since 1999 - barring 2021 due to Covid.

Teams from the nations taking part either qualify or are nominated, before entering the intermediate round, where they are split into eight groups. The winners of those groups then progress to the finals.

Spain have won it four times, Italy three, Poland two, and the Republic of Ireland, Portugal, Croatia and the Czech Republic once each.

On Sunday September 6, McCann and Co fly out to Sweden for three games and the chance to become the first England team ever to progress to the finals.

Who 'England' face and when... Monday September 7: Cheshire League vs Jarvenpaa United, kick-off 3pm UK time

Thursday September 10: Algarve vs Cheshire League, kick-off 3pm UK time

Sunday September 13: Gothenburg vs Cheshire League, kick-off 12pm UK time

"During the Inter-League Cup, the chairman Rob Goodwin-Davey - who is Mr Cheshire League - kept saying to me there was a chance we could go and represent England, but I wasn't really thinking about that. I was purely focused on trying to win the cup," he tells Sky Sports.

"As a management team, we met up a few times to go through final details, tactics, set-pieces and it was then we started to realise it was quite big.

"But once we won it, people in the pub were saying to me: 'Once the World Cup's out the way, you're England manager!'

"Without wanting to compare it too much to 'real life', this job is a bit like being an international manager, albeit a much lower level.

Image: McCann's side will wear official England kit

"I'm sure it will dawn on me when we board the flight, but it's a real privilege and an honour to be England manager for a week, at whatever level. We've worked out we're the England D team, so we'll take that!"

They are not just England by name, though.

"When we get to the airport, we get the full England kit. So whatever you've seen England wearing at the World Cup, it's exactly the same. The boys get a full tracksuit, three t-shirts, three training shirts, three pairs of shorts, three pairs of socks - and we will play in the full England kit.

"A lot of the lads are buzzing for that alone. You have your captains and drivers who are keeping everyone focused on winning the competition, but for some of the lads, just being able to pull the shirt on in a competitive game is massive."

What differentiates the Cheshire League from their professional counterparts, however, is that they are all amateur players with day jobs.

McCann's squad for Sweden AJ Atherton, George Anthony, Callum Burgess, Matt Dixon, Niall Dolan, Amir Hajri, Harry Johnston, Tim Kinsella, Harrison Mather, Liam McDowell, Rob Payne, Rhys Peers, Ben Powell, Matt Saunders, Bailey Sherlock, Lee Simmons, Walker Stone, Arron Woodward.

Among them are captain Tim Kinsella, who is an electrician, and vice-captain Liam McDowell, who is a quantity surveyor. Two members of the squad are qualified PE teachers, others are studying PGCEs to become teachers.

"Some lads are having to take unpaid leave, but the majority are taking it as normal leave and just treating it as an opportunity to have eight days off and enjoy it," McCann adds.

"We haven't had any issues with anyone not able to travel, but it was a concern.

"In the preparation for the final, as a bit of a motivator, I guaranteed the final squad that if we won, they would be the squad I'd take to Sweden. I felt it was right and I've stuck to that.

"The only one missing is Juliano Rosa Silva, who played every minute of the cup, but is injured. He is heartbroken he can't play."

The reality of football at this level is that scouting the opposition is tricky at best.

"For the first game, we've got an FA-registered coach who will be helping out, but his main priority is watching the other teams, so when we play on Monday, he's going to go and watch the other two.

Image: Every member of the final squad bar one will be on the plane to Sweden

"For the second and third games, we'll know a lot more, as I'm sure they will too, and we'll be a lot more prepared. For the first game, we'll be focused on what got us to the King Power and what helped us win it.

"We've built a team that we feel is quite unique in the way we approached it. Without giving too much away, there are probably more technical players in the Cheshire League than what we've picked, but we've picked a team that is to our strengths and we've got a lot of power and pace in the team."

Laying in wait for McCann's side are representative teams from Finland (Jarvenpaa United), Portugal (Algarve) and Sweden (Gothenburg). Of the 34 teams taking part, they are ranked 11th, 7th and 30th respectively; Cheshire League are ranked 17th.

This may be an amateur team, but the preparation for this adventure has been as professional as possible.

"We're just very focused. For now, that's the next step," adds McCann.

Image: No team representing England has ever reached the final stages of the UEFA Regions Cup

"We've done everything we can. We've got the full eight days planned down to the hour. Rest, recovery, recuperation, we've got down the times we're eating, we've mirrored training with game times. If you're going to do it, you do it to the best of your ability.

"In the build-up to the final, Rob got three of the Mid-Cheshire team that won the Inter-League Cup in 2004 to do a speech after the last training session, which was really nice. I met two of them over the summer holidays and asked them about what they felt was good about the trip and I've listened to them and put some things into place.

"We're not going just to enjoy it and be England for seven days, but get beaten. The focus is winning all three games and getting to the finals, but I also see this as a chance to raise the profile for the next generation. It's massive."

Once the trip to Sweden is over, McCann will be back up at the crack of dawn, teaching the next generation - and, all being well, it will be as an England hero… sort of.​​​

Sports.title: Andrews: Brentford are playing with verve - let's see if we can break the ceiling
Sports.content:
Seconds before the curtain came down on the 2025/26 season, Brentford had a golden chance to do what they had never done before: qualify for Europe.

They were drawing 1-1 with Liverpool at Anfield and knew that one goal would be enough to finish seventh and secure Europa League football.

In the 10th minute of added time, Mikkel Damsgaard dropped the ball off to Vitaly Janelt on the left-hand side of the penalty area. The midfielder hit a cross first time that curled in the most inviting way to the centre of the box.

Kevin Schade was waiting for it, but Dango Ouattara got there first - and steered it off target.

Keith Andrews put his head in his hands and sank to his knees. His first season as a head coach had nearly ended in the most perfect way.

"I felt that epitomised the journey we'd been on last season, with how we started the season, how we grew into the season," he says, reflecting on that moment just over three months on.

"Everybody was so engrossed in our journey and gave absolutely everything. There was no shame at all from not getting into Europe, but it whetted the appetite pretty nicely for how we would do things going into pre-season.

"I sat on holiday and had a chance to think about things with immense pride at what we'd achieved. The next thought, very quickly, was how and where we go again."

Image: Andrews was visibly distraught when Dango Ouattara headed over the bar in the final seconds at Anfield

Speaking to Sky Sports that day, he promised improvement in 2026/27. "This is a baseline," he said. "We'll continue to push hard."

Around a fortnight after that Sunday at Anfield, Andrews was back at base.

"There's amazing thinking time you don't normally get on a weekly basis to plan and look at things in a more forensic way," he says.

"You look to improve how we train, how we prepare, what the squad feels like, what the dynamic feels like. Everything where you feel we can get a little bit better.

"I felt like we didn't need huge meetings about what this season will be, I just felt it was there day-to-day. You could smell it, you could feel it."

The first major change came on June 12 with the appointment of his former Republic of Ireland team-mate Damien Duff as his assistant.

Image: Damien Duff spent four years as Shelbourne manager then worked as a FIFA technical advisor before arriving at Brentford

"He's an unbelievable support for me on a daily basis. You've got to be very impactful in your role and whatever responsibilities you have and Damien is certainly that."

The squad planning stage came next and, after an intense summer in 2025, this one was a lot less so.

Star players Bryan Mbeumo and Christian Norgaard were sold to Manchester United and Arsenal respectively, while Yoane Wissa's eventual departure to Newcastle was protracted and disruptive.

There were no headline sales this year. In fact, the only first-team exits were those of Ethan Pinnock - who only played four times in the Premier League last season - and Frank Onyeka - who had spent the best part of two seasons away from west London - to Coventry for less than £12m.

Adding depth, instead, was a key factor in recruitment, which meant Brentford were the eighth-lowest spenders in the Premier League, spending £112.5m.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brentford head coach Keith Andrews speaks on the club's transfer business and process after the summer transfer window closes.

"At certain stages last season, we just lacked that little bit at senior experience in the squad, different options within games to change it," Andrews says.

"We always try to find a way of competing and our players gave absolutely everything last season, but at times they probably needed a little bit more help.

"The way we've gone about our transfers this summer has been very precise. Jannik [Schuster] is a centre-back with a younger age profile and has slotted into the club really well, Callum Wilson and Jaidon Anthony have proven Premier League quality with experience, so it's not just on the pitch, it's off it in terms of what they bring.

"Mamadou Sangare was an eye-catching signing and he's started really well in our shirt. And the latest one is Malick [Diouf] from West Ham, who we were delighted to be able to get into the building.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Keith Andrews says El Hadji Malick Diouf 'fits what we are about' as he joins Brentford for 40 million from West Ham.

"We've added to an already really good squad, we've added very well and we've kept hold of exactly who we wanted to keep hold of. I'm really, really happy with the deals we've got done."

Andrews often speaks about getting better - and is open about the fact that getting better than last season means reaching Europe: "Naturally, the next step for us is to try and break that ceiling."

He will, no doubt, field questions on that topic in press conferences for many months to come.

But what does that look like in action?

"The next level of development of individuals," he says.

"Pick a player… Michael Kayode. He had an amazing season, let's get him better. You make all your players better, you feed them that confidence, you create that environment, which we do create. It's inevitable if someone is as humble and hungry as Michael, they will get better.

Image: Michael Kayode (left) has been a key player for Brentford since arriving from Fiorentina in January 2025

"Players getting better naturally improves the team. Then you look at each phase of the game.

"At set-pieces we look a real threat, we look really dominant at the moment and we want to continue that.

"How do we create chances? The game is about scoring at one end and keeping goals out at the other, so how do you create opportunities? We want to create opportunities in different ways and not just be a predictable team that can only do it one way.

"And how do we become better without the ball? Are we pressing aggressively high? Can we sit in deep and absorb pressure and be a transition threat, but defend our box with aggression and collective spirit?

"They are just some examples about how we want to take the next step."

So far, that next step is beginning to take shape.

On the opening weekend, they welcomed Tottenham to the Gtech Community Stadium - and blew Roberto De Zerbi's side away.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Brentford and Tottenham Hotspur.

They won 3-0, but it would have been four had Igor Thiago not rolled his penalty onto the base of the left-hand post.

Analysing the game afterwards, Sky Sports' Jamie Redknapp was impressed by what he saw.

"When somebody was out of position, they just found a way to fill the right areas. They are incredibly brave at the back, the two centre-backs play so high and press you, stop you getting out," he said.

"What Roberto De Zerbi said beforehand was that they were going to deal with a lot of long balls today, but what they actually dealt with was total football.

"It can mean different things when I hear that said," Andrews responds.

"When I think about that in terms of how we play the game, we can play in different ways. We can control games now with the ability we have as a team, the quality we have technically as a team.

"The individuals are flourishing within the squad and how we're playing, then if teams want to have a fight, we'll have a fight.

"We've got so many different attributes within the squad where we can cause the opposition problems in an unpredictable way, but we always respect every phase of the game and try and respect the opposition where we try to nullify their strengths and see if we can outdo them."

Coco Gauff was given a stern test against Spain's Paula ‌Badosa before ultimately securing a 6-4 7-6 (7-5) victory.

The American fourth seed and 2023 US Open winner continues her path to the third round, where she will face ​Spaniard Cristina Bucsa.

On a sweltering evening that contrasted with the rain-hit opening days, Gauff took to Arthur ​Ashe Court with the backing of a partisan crowd and hopes of continuing her pursuit of a third Grand Slam title.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the US Open match between Paula Badosa and Coco Gauff..

But it ​was no simple task against the world No 87, ‌who, despite the gulf in the rankings, holds a positive record over the American, including victories in ​their last two meetings - a straight-sets win at last year's Australian Open first round and more recently, during this summer's grass-court swing in Berlin.

Badosa threatened early to seize the initiative, forcing Gauff to save two break points. But the American struck with ‌the decisive break, aided by a costly forehand error from the Spaniard that appeared to rattle her both mentally and in her execution, as Gauff closed out ‌the opener to take the lead.

I was ​a bit upset watching everybody practice preparing for the tournament ​and I was just doing all possible recovery and gym. I'm super happy to be here."

Zverev edges late-night thriller to avoid early exit

Alexander Zverev survived another huge scare by coming through his latest five-set thriller and late-night victory to beat Quentin Halys at the US Open.

Image: Alexander Zverev is through to the third round of the US Open after another five-set thriller

The top seed was taken the distance by Lorenzo Sonego in the opening round and faced the same situation against Halys, having twice surrendered a set lead in the Arthur Ashe ‌Stadium.

Zverev eventually claimed a 6-4 4-6 ‌7-6(3) 6-7(3) 6-3 victory, in a match that lasted over four and a half hours and didn't finish until 2.15am local time (7.15am UK time), to book a third-round meeting with Alejandro Tabilo.

The French Open champion becomes the first top-seeded man to start a major with back-to-back five-set matches in the Open Era, which dates to 1968.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Quentin Halys pulled off this terrific shot during his game against Alexander Zverev at the US Open

"The performance was quite s***, to be honest," said Zverev in his on-court interview. "But, I won, and that's the most important thing. I've been here for another four and a half hours.

"That's what I go to the gym for, that's what I go to the track for and that's what I train for, to be able to come out on top in these difficult moments. When you're not playing your best, when you're not hitting winners left and right, just getting through these matches.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alexander Zverev was booed for requesting a racket change at around 2am during his US Open match against Quentin Halys before a frank assessment of his own performance

"I hope at some point I'll start playing better but, for now, I'm happy to be in the third round."

Tien too good as Monfils makes final Grand Slam bow

Young American Learner Tien brought the ‌curtain down on Gael Monfils' Grand Slam career on Thursday as ‌the American youngster defeated the French veteran 6-3 6-4 ​6-3 in a clash of generations to reach the third ​round.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the US Open match between Gael Monfils and Learner Tien.

Monfils turned back the clock ‌to beat Adolfo Daniel Vallejo in the first round on ​his 40th birthday and extend his stay in New York, but the wildcard's run ended under ​lights against an opponent half ⁠his age.

On a muggy evening Monfils appeared ‌drained towards the end of the first set and turned to the crowd for inspiration, but ‌14th seed Tien was unfazed and tightened his grip on the contest.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gael Monfils has revealed what he plans on doing after retiring from Tennis, having lost to Learner Tien in the second round of the US Open

With the opening set in the bag, 20-year-old Tien continued to dictate ⁠proceedings in the next, absorbing Monfils' ​bursts of aggression to clinch it ​and edge closer to the third ​round for a meeting with Czech Jakub Mensik.

Monfils ⁠made a final, emotion-fuelled charge in the third set with some trademark shot-making, but Tien ⁠stood his ground and sealed ​victory before warmly embracing the French showman ​who will retire at the end of the year.

Sports.title: Kyrgios accepts one-month suspension after positive cocaine test
Sports.content:
Nick Kyrgios has accepted ‌and served a reduced, one-month suspension under anti-doping rules after testing positive ‌for cocaine at an ATP Tour event in ​Mallorca.

Kyrgios, who had been ​provisionally suspended since August 4, had ‌entered into a treatment programme approved by the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) to ​reduce the three-month default suspension under WADA rules.

The Australian gave a sample at an ATP tournament in Majorca in June which tested positive for benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gigi Salmon is joined by Annabel Croft and Ryan Harrison to react to the news that Kyrgios tested positive for cocaine and been suspended from the sport

The drug is banned in competition and the former Wimbledon finalist has been provisionally suspended since August 4, meaning he cannot play or attend tournaments.

During an ​interview with ITIA investigators, the 31-year-old ⁠explained that his use ⁠of cocaine had "occurred socially" during a night out before he was due ‌to play in Mallorca, the statement said.

The ITIA consulted an independent scientific expert at a ‌World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)-accredited laboratory, who stated that the explanation was consistent with the level of cocaine found in his sample.

"As a result, the ITIA accepted ⁠that Kyrgios' use of cocaine was ​outside of competition," it added.

The ITIA ​said Kyrgios' suspension ends on Thursday, ​subject to completion of the programme.

Prize money and ⁠ranking points from the Mallorca event will be forfeited.

Cocaine is prohibited in-competition and carries a ⁠provisional suspension.

Kyrgios apologised last month ​on social media for the failed drug ​test, saying he had made a "huge mistake" and took full responsibility for ‌it.

"I made a huge mistake and I take full responsibility for it," Kyrgios said in a post on Instagram.

"I'm sorry to my fans, my family, my sponsors and everyone close to me. Above all, I'm sorry to the kids who follow me. I know the example this sets and I'm deeply disappointed in myself."

His first-round loss to fellow Australian Adam Walton in Majorca was his last competitive singles outing and one of only four singles matches he has played this season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the 'Battle of the Sexes' match between Aryna Sabalenka and Kyrgios

'Tormented soul' Kyrgios in firing line

Sky Sports Tennis' Annabel Croft described Kyrgios as a "tormented soul" who could now find himself on the receiving end of the very criticism he dished out when Jannik Sinner and Iga Swiatek were involved in high-profile doping cases.

"He has always struck me as a tormented soul out there, and he is never far from creating headlines," Croft said. "He seems to do that effortlessly.

"There is a lot of criticism being thrown at him right now because he was the one firing arrows at other players who had been banned for a certain amount of time. It is now being directed right back at him."

'Kyrgios needs to find balance'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at some of Kyrgios' best points of his ATP career

Former world No 40 Ryan Harrison believes Kyrgios must strike the right balance between his responsibilities on the court and his downtime off it.

"It is disappointing," Harrison added. "Kyrgios has been such an electric player for so long.

"He is one of those guys. You talk about the 'Big Four', and he was the next in line that the casual fan and observer would talk about because of the way he played, his talent, fearlessness and energy.

"The persona would come out sometimes in the way he handled pressure. Sometimes it wasn't always positive.

"When you are an athlete and training on a regular basis, your life is very structured and regimented.

"When you stop playing and you are not doing that on a week-to-week basis, some players can find it difficult to strike a balance and know, 'When can I go out?'

"I think Nick needs to find that balance and, while it is disappointing, hopefully for his sake, as he takes time away, he can find happiness off the court and be the best he can be."

4m ago 07.01 EDT Frank Lampard says his Coventry side will have to get used to that losing feeling this season. The Sky Blues have endured a tough return to the Premier League with back-to-back losses against Arsenal and Hull and things do not get any easier this weekend as they travel to Manchester City. Speaking ahead of Coventry’s trip to his former club, Lampard has warned his players they need to pick themselves up after defeats: double quotation mark I think we all know that it will not look like last season, and the quicker we realise that the better, because last season was an incredible season for us because we won a lot and everything becomes easier in that moment. So it’s important that we understand the rigours of the Premier League, how it may feel different and that mindset has to be clear on that to be able to get up after a difficult result like Hull in whatever way or shape it may come. We train well through the week, prepare for the next one. Share

17m ago 06.49 EDT Crystal Palace are still searching for their first point under Pierre Sage, but the new man in charge does at least still have Adam Wharton to call on after another deadlne day passed without the midfielder leaving. Sage described Wharton as “really smart” for prolonging his career at Selhurst Park after Palace rejected offers from clubs in England and around Europe for the 22-year-old. Ahead of Saturday’s derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, Sage said: double quotation mark The club was strong with his situation and the player is completely in line with that. He never spoke with me about a possible departure, that’s why I think he is in a project to manage his career and he is really smart to do it like this. He did the job every day without a bad mindset and that’s why I understood quickly he wanted to stay and prepare his future with us. 2h ago 05.33 EDT Hackett: 'Dean in fantasy land over podcast claims' Mike Dean’s former boss insists the referee would not have been able to play the “games” he claims to have done while officiating. Dean, who refereed in the Premier League until 2022, generated controversy after claiming on the ‘Jamie Vardy’s Having a Party’ podcast he would “joke about” during matches, seeing how long he could go without blowing his whistle or leaving the centre circle. Keith Hackett, Dean’s former boss at Professional Game Match Officials Limited (PGMOL) between 2004 and 2010, insisted he could not have got away with doing so. Hackett wrote on X: “Mike Dean is in fantasy land!! The examination of performances assessors is forensic. When I was boss referee’s performances were forensically examined. 2h ago 05.03 EDT Matt Hughes Broadcasters and governing bodies make tax plea for TV coverage of women’s sport The chief executives of the Football Association, Rugby Football Union and England and Wales Cricket Board have joined forces with leading broadcasters and YouTube in writing to the chancellor requesting tax credits for production companies to help deliver more television coverage of women’s sport. In a letter signed by 25 representatives of the country’s biggest sports and broadcasters, including Sky Sports and ITV, the government is urged to extend to women’s sport production the audio-visual expenditure credit scheme that provides tax relief to independent films and children’s television. The joint letter, was sent to John Healey on Friday to coincide with this weekend’s return of the Women’s Super League, whose chief executive, Nikki Doucet, is among the signatories, along with the bosses of British Cycling, golf and Formula One. The WSL is the second-richest league in women’s sport after National Women’s Soccer League in the US, but faces challenges attracting broadcasters in a congested market. 2h ago 04.56 EDT Richarlison omitted from Tottenham’s Premier League squad Richarlison may have played his last match for Tottenham after he was left out of the club’s 25-man Premier League squad list on Thursday. Spurs manager Roberto De Zerbi, speaking following a 2-0 home defeat by Newcastle on Saturday, insisted Richarlison had “said too many times he wants to leave” and could bid farewell to the London club before the summer transfer window closed. The Brazil forward released an incendiary social media post on Monday where he claimed “never again will anyone decide my future for me”. Talks over a potential return to Premier League rivals Everton, where he played from 2018 to 2022, stalled before Tuesday’s deadline in England. Other transfer windows around the world remain open, however, and Trabzonspor have been linked with Richarlison ahead of today’s deadline in Turkey. Richarlison, who currently remains a Spurs player, made his feelings clear on Monday, with a remarkable outburst on Instagram. Agence France-Presse View image in fullscreen Richarlison looks to have played his final game for Spurs. Photograph: Shaun Brooks/CameraSport/Getty Images Share Updated at 06.46 EDT

3h ago 04.33 EDT Tom Garry On the eve of the new WSL season, London City Lionesses have done their biggest deal to date… View image in fullscreen London City Lionesses have announced a landmark multi-year front-of-shirt partnership with Nike. Photograph: London City Lionesses The Women’s Super League club London City Lionesses’ new front-of-shirt sponsorship deal with Nike is the largest in the women’s game, according to their American owner, Michele Kang. It has been reported that the largest current front-of-shirt sponsorship deal for a women’s football team is an approximately $4m per year agreement reached by the new NWSL franchise in Atlanta – who will begin competing in 2028, but Kang told BBC Sport: “I can absolutely confirm that this is the largest women-only front-of-shirt deal. It is higher than the Atlanta number. “I can absolutely also share that it is higher than some of the men’s Premier League front-of-shirt deals. It’s huge. That’s why it is landmark. There are so many other people who believe in the future of women’s football. They [Nike] didn’t make this decision lightly. They did not write a charity cheque. They believe in the future and they believe together we will invest and build this future together.” More details: London City claim sponsor deal is record and bigger than some in Premier League Read more Share Updated at 04.35 EDT

3h ago 04.24 EDT Liverpool sign young St Etienne winger N’Guessan Andy Hunter Liverpool have signed St Etienne winger Djylian N’Guessan as part of their drive to add highly-rated young talent to their ranks. The 18-year-old, who made his senior St Etienne debut at 16, has signed a pre-contract agreement that will see him officially become a Liverpool player in January. He has cost €5m and St Etienne secured a sell-on clause. N’Guessan will now spend the first half of the season on loan at Brest before Liverpool review his next step in January. N’Guessan’s signature follows the £30m deal for goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans to arrive from Genk next summer and other signings identified by Liverpool’s global talent team in the last 12 months - Armin Pecsi, Mor Talla Ndiaye, Ifeanyi Ndukwe and Samuel Martinez. 3h ago 04.16 EDT Barry Glendenning More on Dean’s loose lips from Barry Glendenning in yesterday’s Football Daily: Dean appears to blow the whistle on himself over in-match game claims While Football Daily likes to think we have our finger on the cultural pulse, before this week we were oblivious to the fact that Jamie Vardy has his own podcast. Called Jamie Vardy’s Having a Party, it is a far more sedate affair than the name suggests, given the only episode we have seen features our t1tular hero and his sidekick the comedian Josh James listening to Mike Dean reminisce about his time as a referee. While Football Daily can’t think of any social gathering that wouldn’t be enhanced by the presence of a 61-year-old former match official from the Wirral on its guest list, this isn’t so much a party as an occasionally awkward conversation. Its claim to be “a hilarious look back at Mike’s career at the heart of English football” is as bold as it is false, but what the episode lacks in laughs it has more than made up for in controversy. During the course of the chat, Dean revealed to his hosts that in the pre-VAR era he and his assistants used to keep themselves amused by playing little games within games of top-flight football. “We used to say: ‘Right, we’ll kick off now, right? See how long we can go without blowing a whistle’. Done that a few times in the Premier, before VAR obviously. Went 20-25 minutes without blowing a whistle a few times. Let it go, let it go, let it go.” Dean went on to tell his inquisitors that he also used to see how long he could go without leaving the centre-circle while games were being played around him, claiming that he once set up camp in one for almost 15 minutes. “That was just me joking about,” he honked, promptly eliciting not entirely convincing laughs from a clearly surprised Josh and Jamie. Read the Football Daily in full: Football Daily | Mike Dean appears to blow the whistle on himself over in-match game claims Read more Share

3h ago 04.11 EDT I thought nonsense and transfers were over for a while, alas. Dean claims he played secret games for a laugh while refereeing matches View image in fullscreen Mike Dean stood down as a referee in 2022. Photograph: Adrian Dennis/AFP/Getty Images The former Premier League referee Mike Dean claims he used to take part in secret challenges while officiating, including trying to stay in the centre circle for as long as possible, as he confessed to “just joking about” during matches. The remarks, made by one of the most well-known officials in the English game, have been met with bemusement by refereeing officials who say there is no evidence of any such behaviour having ever taken place. Dean was a member of the select group of referees for more than two decades before he retired in 2022 and a brief spell as a video assistant referee followed. In an interview on Jamie Vardy’s podcast this week, Dean shared anecdotes from his time as a top-flight official in the pre-VAR era. “We used to say, ‘We’ll kick off now. Right, see how long we can go without blowing a whistle,’” he said. “I’ve done that a few times in the Premier League, before VAR obviously – [I] went 20, 25 minutes without blowing a whistle. “I used to do another thing. I used to stand in the centre circle – see how long I could stay in the centre circle before I had to leave. That was just me joking about. I got about 15 minutes once.” Officials within the refereeing organisation, Pro Ref, are understood to be puzzled by the claims, with the suggestion that a referee could stay in the centre circle for 15 minutes without someone noticing, for example, seen as highly improbable.
