Sports.title: Nottingham Forest’s Liam Delap: ‘I play at my best on the edge of being horrible’
Sports.content:
“You can imagine it: he’s a centre-back, I’m a striker,” says Liam Delap, Nottingham Forest’s £45m club-record signing, smiling as he sets the scene. He is reliving taking on his younger brother, Finn, in the garden. These days, they are each other’s biggest supporters – Liam attended Finn’s victory for third-tier Burton on Wednesday – but as kids there was a friendly rivalry. “There were probably a lot of tears, a lot of fights … whether it was playing Monopoly or football, it always ended in either the table being flipped or kicking the shit out of each other.”

It is a competitive streak that has stuck and Delap is determined to make his presence felt at Forest, for whom he could make his full debut against Tottenham on Saturday. It has been a testing 16 months; he left Chelsea a season into a six-year contract and after one goal in 28 top-flight appearances, a dozen of those starts. “It is never a linear path straight to the top,” Delap says, his right hand taking flight in the City Ground boardroom, the 1979 and 1980 European Cups shimmering behind him. “I just want to get my head down, focus and keep improving because I’m still so young and I have so much to learn. I even at times probably think I’ve been in football a lot longer than I have. I’ve still, hopefully, got a long career ahead.

“I think you just have to accept that sometimes things go bad, things happen … it might [prove to] be a good thing, I think. My first loans to Stoke and Preston [across 2022-23] didn’t really go well at all and it was probably one of the best things that happened because I learnt so much from that season and went to Hull [for 2023-24] and kicked on from there. I’m still young, I’ve still got a lot of learning to do. Sometimes injuries happen, sometimes you don’t play. I don’t think anything is lost … Everyone has rocky moments. I’ve just got to use them to learn and kick on.”

Last summer, Delap was hot property. Oliver Glasner tells a story of Delap having proposals from 18 Premier League clubs and jests that the 23-year-old knows every top-flight manager owing to the various Zoom calls he held while deciding his next move. After all, one of those was with Glasner, then at Crystal Palace. Forest wanted him then, too. “It was a tough decision,” recalls Delap. “I remember the conversation we had, I was really impressed and I thought: ‘This guy [Glasner] is really good.’ He spoke incredibly well and you can see he has done really well with the strikers he has had in the past. That definitely stuck in my mind.”

Glasner wants Delap to play to his strengths: physicality, power and finishing. He doesn’t mean the forward’s hidden talent: cube roots. At the start of the year a clip of Delap showing off his maths skills went viral. “I didn’t enjoy maths one bit but I was always quite good at it. One of my friends taught me in school how to do it and I didn’t forget it. I hated school, [the] work, but I was always quite intelligent.”

The Austrian head coach said it was apparent in conversations with Delap this summer that the player had learnt lessons from a trying year: “I think it shows his attitude and his character that he said: ‘Yeah, I want a team and a club that values my strengths and wants to play to my strengths.’ Because I never want to change a player: it doesn’t make sense to say: ‘OK, now you should play like Messi: false nine, drop into midfield and combine play with one or two touches.”

View image in fullscreen Liam Delap scored once in 28 league appearances for Chelsea. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

A tally of 12 goals in the Ipswich side relegated in 2024-25 triggered widespread interest. At that point, Delap was talked up as a potential heir to Harry Kane as England’s No 9. He has been capped by his country at every age group and was in the same under-16s team as Jude Bellingham. “As a little kid, all you want to do is play for your country. So, of course, in my mind that’s where I want to get to. But it’s not as easy as that. I have to work hard and improve and that’s all I can do.”

An imposing 6ft 2in striker, Delap has long been viewed as the next big thing. He spearheaded Manchester City to FA Youth Cup victory over Chelsea in 2020, a couple of months after Pep Guardiola handed him his senior City debut aged 17. Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, now teammates at Chelsea, were part of that same under-18s side, together with the new Aston Villa defender Taylor Harwood-Bellis and James McAtee, one of his best friends and now a clubmate.

“He was a No 10 and quite often he would give me the ball and we just had that really good relationship off the pitch and it translated on to the pitch,” Delap says of McAtee. “If we didn’t win, we’d all be fuming. It probably instilled that winning mentality into us early. I think it’s worked because you can see from that team that almost everyone is playing somewhere in the Premier League, abroad, the Championship and that is probably because we pushed each other so much.”

Delap made his Forest debut as a substitute at Anfield last weekend, his first notable action a quick throw-in that led to the penalty scored by Morgan Gibbs-White to earn a second-half lead. Only after the 2-2 draw did Glasner discover that Delap’s father, Rory, who played for Southampton and Stoke, among others, knew a thing or two about throws. “I said: your father will be proud of you,” says Forest’s head coach. So, has Liam got a mammoth throw in his armoury? “No, I don’t think so,” he replies. “I would never, anyway: I’m a striker, I need to be in the box.”

Delap relishes the blood and thunder of battle. Glasner loves how Forest’s marquee signing stands up to centre-backs, making the point that defenders are hardly “hugging and kissing you all the time” in the heat of duels. But Delap, who spent a decade at Derby before joining City, says he has learned to harness his aggression on the field, after periods of getting into trouble when he was a youngster.

View image in fullscreen Liam Delap was much in demand after impressing with Ipswich. Photograph: Ryan Pierse/Getty Images

“You have to be careful, but not shy away from who you are,” he says. “I’m always going to fight for everything, always be aggressive, determined. It goes back to the point about my brother, being little kids in the garden, going at each other: that’s me. Sometimes you need to control it and sometimes you need to be careful, but I think I play at my best when I’m on that edge of being … being horrible.”

Sports.title: Manchester City failed to land Spain pair in scramble for Miedema cover
Sports.content:
Atlético Madrid rejected a bid of more than £500,000 from Manchester City for the Spain midfielder Fiamma Benítez on the Women’s Super League’s transfer deadline day, the Guardian can reveal.

The WSL champions are understood to have tried hard to add attacking-midfielder reinforcements before the English summer window closed on Thursday at 11pm BST, largely in light of news that their No 10 Vivianne Miedema could be out for at least the rest of 2026 with a knee injury.

However, Atlético are understood to view Benítez as a key player and a future national team star and were not prepared to let the 22-year-old go. In 2022 Benítez helped Spain win the Under-19 Euros and Under-20 Women’s World Cup and she helped her country win the 2024 Women’s Nations League.

City then made an even later move for Everton’s Spain international Ornella Vignola, who can play in midfield or on the wing. A bid of about £400,000 is understood to have been turned down by Everton, largely because they felt they would not have time to source a suitable replacement but also because of Vignola’s importance to Scott Phelan’s side.

It was also widely reported that City attempted to bring in the Nigeria midfielder Jennifer Echegini from Paris Saint-Germain, but multiple sources have told the Guardian that PSG made clear they were not willing to sell the 25-year-old. PSG had agreed to sell the France defender Élisa De Almeida to Arsenal for a fee believed to be just over £500,000, and they were not prepared to lose two key players in one day.

City completed one deadline-day deal, bringing in England’s Anna Moorhouse on loan from Orlando Pride until the end of January, adding good-quality depth to their goalkeeping ranks after Khiara Keating moved to Liverpool on a free in July.

Although City were left scrambling unsuccessfully for a midfielder on Thursday, it was a positive summer for the club, not least because they began the summer with their most important deal, retaining the services of the WSL’s Golden Boot winner Khadija Shaw with a lucrative new contract. Andrée Jeglertz’s side begin their title defence at home to promoted Birmingham City on Sunday.

Manchester City, Chelsea and Arsenal will discover their Women’s Champions League league phase opponents on Friday, with the draw due to begin at 11am BST.

Sports.title: Women’s Super League Q&A: ask football writer Suzanne Wrack a question ahead of the new season
Sports.content:
4h ago 03.04 EDT Welcome to the Conversation

The Women’s Super League season kicks off tonight with London City Lionesses versus Manchester United. The 2026/27 marks an exciting new era for women’s football with an expansion to 14 teams, the introduction of playoffs, increased investment and some huge transfers.

Suzanne Wrack has been reporting on women’s football for the Guardian since 2017, appears on our Women’s Football Weekly podcast and is the author of the award winning A Woman’s Game: The Rise, Fall, and Rise Again of Women’s Football. She will be here at 1pm BST/8am ET to answer your questions. Will London City’s superstar signing Alexia Putellas be the magic bullet? How will newly promoted Birmingham City, Charlton Athletic and Crystal Palace fair? Can Manchester City go back to back?

Ask a question: log in or sign up here and post your question in the comments below.

In the meantime, here is Suzanne’s introduction to the season and some recent interviews.

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
Sports.content:
1 Can Wirtz find his best for Liverpool?

Florian Wirtz is easing himself into his second season at Liverpool after a forgettable first. There were signs of promise against Nottingham Forest, where he set up the second equaliser and would have had a goal of his own if not for an offside in the buildup. It is clear the German needs to become more influential as a No 10 given the quality of players he has around him, especially after the expensive arrival of Bradley Barcola this week. Bruno Fernandes showed there is plenty of fun for an attacking midfielder to have against Ipswich and Wirtz can follow suit as a protagonist. Liverpool have drawn both their opening fixtures 2-2 and need something to kickstart their campaign, with a Friday night visit to promoted opposition a fine place to do so. Wirtz should cause problems but, if he does not, the internal competition will be after his spot. Will Unwin

Ipswich v Liverpool (Friday 8pm, all times BST)

2 Red Bull gives you wings

Verticality, intensity and hard pressing are likely to be the order of the day at St James’ Park, where two German graduates of the Red Bull stable meet on Saturday at lunchtime. Newcastle’s new manager, Matthias Jaissle, is a former head coach of Red Bull Salzburg, while Bournemouth’s Marco Rose has managed Salzburg and RB Leipzig. “We have the same idea of how we want to play football,” said Jaissle – and Rose knows what to expect from Eddie Howe’s successor. “Matthias and me were several years in the style of Red Bull,” he said. “Everyone knows how we work. You can see it clearly. He’s a good coach. He’s brought his ideas really quickly into the Newcastle team. They are playing quite intense, they have clear pressing patterns that are different from before.” Louise Taylor

Newcastle v Bournemouth (Saturday 12.30pm)

View image in fullscreen Matthias Jaissle is looking for back-to-back league wins with Newcastle. Photograph: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

3 Bees plot left-wing raid on Black Cats

Saturday’s meeting between two of the Premier League’s best-run clubs, Brentford and Sunderland, promises to one of the best contests of the weekend, with both sides physical, technical and superbly coached. Brentford, in particular, have made a terrific start to the season, the left side of their team looking especially dangerous. Keane Lewis-Potter provides impetus from full-back, with Mamadou Sangaré backing up strong ball-winning and carrying with intelligent passing, while Kevin Schade offers a threat in behind and, increasingly, in front of goal. All of which suggests a difficult afternoon for Thomas Meunier, Sunderland’s likely right-back who, at 34, has plenty of experience but might struggle with the athletic questions asked of him. He will, though, be able to rely on assistance from Noah Sadiki, whose nous, work ethic and running power will be invaluable in defending Sunderland’s right flank. How that battle plays out will go a long way towards deciding the game. Daniel Harris

Brentford v Sunderland (Saturday 3pm)

4 Chema looks another astute Brighton buy

We can be sure any player Brighton buy has delivered the data metrics employed by the owner, Tony Bloom. But Chema Andrés, the 21-year-old midfielder just signed from Stuttgart, also nails the eye test. He was signed for £18.9m and it’s already tempting to speculate how sizeable the mark-up will be when Brighton sell him on. If we remember we’re talking about a sport, it’s impossible not to be excited about what the former Real Madrid academy midfielder brings to Fabian Hürzeler’s team. A No 6 of the old school, Chema offers economical movement but extravagant intelligence, evident in his passing and anticipation. Even if this weekend’s game against Leeds comes too early for him to be handed a start, he will make an impact soon enough. DH

Brighton v Leeds (Saturday 3pm)

5 An early basement battle at the Cottage

It’s been a tricky summer for Crystal Palace despite their Conference League win. Oliver Glasner has gone, with two key defenders in Daniel Muñoz and Maxence Lacroix also departing and Jean-Philippe Mateta and Ismaïla Sarr trying their best to do likewise. This upheaval has left Pierre Sage, whose existing relationship with Malick Fofana wasn’t enough to secure the Lyon winger’s signature, with major problems. The former Lens coach is seeking to replace the club’s most successful manager while learning what works in a new league, with new players and without three mainstays. It wasn’t especially surprising to see Palace lose their first two matches, while Fulham have also been beaten twice while seeking to bed in a new coach and arrivals. More troubling for both teams is that the promoted sides look competitive. Hull and Ipswich have performed well and won games, while Coventry are better than they’ve shown so far. Though it’s far too early to talk about relegation, this already feels like a game of significance for two sides struggling for momentum. DH

Fulham v Crystal Palace (Saturday 3pm)

6 O’Reilly to step into Rodri role for City?

Manchester City spent more than £300m on new midfielders in this transfer window, but look light in the No 6 role, with Rodri and Nico González both departing. Ayyoub Bouaddi, bought as Rodri’s long-term successor, is only 18, so Enzo Maresca’s plan is to ease him into first-team action. The Manchester City manager deployed Marc Guéhi in a holding midfield role against Bournemouth, and is also confident Nico O’Reilly can switch from left-back to operate there. O’Reilly may line up at the base of midfield for Coventry’s visit, with City seeking a third straight win. Maresca is also not fazed by Omar Marmoush’s departure on an initial loan to Spurs, with Iliman Ndiaye arriving on deadline day and Antoine Semenyo also an able deputy centre-forward if Erling Haaland is unavailable. Jamie Jackson

Manchester City v Coventry (Saturday 3pm)

7 Delap to be thrown in against shaky Spurs

Liam Delap came off the bench against Liverpool and helped create Nottingham Forest’s second goal with quick thinking from a throw-in. The striker cost £45m from Chelsea but missed out on an intense pre-season after Xabi Alonso decided he was surplus to requirements, so needs to build fitness. Considering Tottenham’s major flaws thus far, it would make sense for Delap to be given the chance to spearhead the Forest attack. The former England Under-21s striker is the ideal No 9, quick, strong and a capable finisher, but needs to get all these attributes sharpened up. An outing against fragile opposition could speed up the process. Tottenham are bottom of the league having conceded five and scored none in two games, and compared with Chris Wood or Igor Jesus, Delap is a far scarier foe, as Oliver Glasner will know. WU

Nottingham Forest v Tottenham (Saturday 3pm)

8 Six points, seven signings for happy Hull

They may have nabbed two wins in as many games upon their return to the Premier League but Hull were still not happy with their squad, seven new players arriving in the final week of the window. That means the Tigers have made 19 signings since promotion, which is an impressive turnover in personnel. Sergej Jakirovic needs to decide whether to incorporate these potential upgrades into his starting XI as soon as possible or make them earn the shirts from those who have accumulated six points. No one has let down the head coach or the fans over 180 minutes, so it would be harsh to drop anyone but, equally, having spent so much money on acquisitions, it could be argued that the sooner they get on the pitch, the quicker they will gel. It is not an easy decision for Jakirovic to make but he values loyalty and will want to challenge the mentality of the new arrivals – no one will walk into the side he has built. WU

Hull v Aston Villa (Saturday 5.30pm)

View image in fullscreen Elliot Stroud, one of Hull’s 19 summer signings, in action during their 1-0 win at Coventry. Photograph: Neal Simpson/Getty Images/Allstar

9 Everton fans react to dismal deadline day

There are parallels between Manchester United’s visit to Hill Dickinson Stadium and their 3-0 win at Goodison Park in 2023 in the sense they will face a furious Everton crowd, and for the second time in four seasons the anger will not be directed towards them. Three years ago it was the Premier League in Evertonians’ sights after the record 10-point deduction that had just been imposed on the club. This time it is Everton’s owners, The Friedkin Group, in the firing line after the club’s shambolic end to the transfer window. There will be no flag displays inside the stadium after the group responsible for organising them, the 1878s, withdrew their support and there are calls for a “not a pound in the ground” campaign in response to the owners making a profit on transfers while leaving David Moyes with a weaker squad. Everton have started the season positively on the pitch, but are now surrounded by problems of their owners’ making. Andy Hunter

Everton v Manchester United (Sunday 2pm)

10 Chelsea face litmus test in London derby

You have to go back to the start of the 2021-22 season, when Arsenal had Rob Holding and Pablo Marí in central defence, for the last time Chelsea beat their north London rivals, a run of 11 matches in all competitions. But they came close to ending that sequence in the 1-1 draw at Stamford Bridge last season before things began to unravel for Enzo Maresca, and the Italian’s successor, Xabi Alonso, will head to the Emirates to face his old friend Mikel Arteta in a competitive match for the first time as a manager full of confidence after winning his opening two games. Chelsea’s new-look front three of Cole Palmer, João Pedro and Morgan Rogers can certainly cause Arsenal problems, although the question is whether a defence that has conceded five goals can keep out the champions. Ed Aarons

Arsenal v Chelsea (Sunday 4.30pm)

Sports.title: Tough start for PSG but Luis Enrique has faith in burst of ‘new energy’ from signings
Sports.content:
“It’s like we’re at school,” Luis Enrique quipped as he entered the press conference room, hearing the journalists respond in unison to his hearty bonjour.

His remark was fitting on the eve of Paris Saint-Germain’s first home match of the season, which lines up nicely with France’s rentrée, the term for the nationwide return to school and the office at the start of September. Although the new campaign is in full swing by now, the team have had to wait several weeks before making their return to the Parc des Princes, where they welcome second place Monaco on Friday night.

The league champions were due to start the season by hosting Rennes on the first day, but successive heatwaves over the summer had damaged the Parc des Princes pitch to the extent that the match was instead moved to Brittany. Rennes were also hoping to host the return match in March as scheduled, but the league authorities instead switched the two fixtures around in the calendar.

This year’s rentrée has not exactly seen a swift return to business as usual for the perennial Ligue 1 champions. Since beating Aston Villa to retain the Uefa Super Cup last month, PSG have lost the Trophée des Champions to Lens and drawn their first two league matches.

Late comebacks in the latter two fixtures have helped paper over the cracks of unconvincing displays against the league’s middle powers. A late double from Ferran Torres on debut rescued a point against Rennes, while a Vitinha-led revival saw PSG claw back a similar deficit in stoppage time in Lille.

“We’ve had less of a pre-season, so it’s been difficult,” summer signing Lucas Digne explained on Thursday after an open training session. “It’s not an excuse, but it’s an assessment.”

Admittedly, PSG’s first four domestic opponents of the season will have all been teams involved in Europe. “It hasn’t been the easiest combination of matches,” the head coach, Luis Enrique, said in his press conference later in the day. “But we’ve had to accept it and prepare for them.”

View image in fullscreen Ferran Torres scored twice on his PSG debut to rescue a point against Rennes. Photograph: Franco Arland/Getty Images

PSG now habitually click into gear mid-season, once the Champions League knockouts begin to appear on the horizon. A defeat to Monaco on Friday, though, could spark a minor crisis and precipitate the need for the team to be back at their full powers.

In any case, Luis Enrique was cryptic when asked about when his team would be at their best: “It depends on a lot of factors which are out of my control,” he said. “My job is just to find the best 11 players for each match.” The fact that his reigning champions are winless in three has ostensibly done little to dampen the 56-year-old’s optimism for his fourth season in charge.

“Do you think that losing tomorrow means we’re out of the title race?” Luis Enrique asked reporters on Thursday afternoon. “Our aim will be to beat a team that we lost to at home last season. It won’t be easy, especially considering they have a manager in Filipe Luís who takes a brave approach.”

View image in fullscreen The Paris Saint-Germain head coach, Luis Enrique, is hoping his team will be back to their best when they host Monaco. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

The Spaniard was also keen to stress the minor squad overhaul which took place over the summer. “We haven’t sold any of the players who started the Champions League final and we’ve bought some young players. We’ll have to wait and see what they can bring.”

While the starting XI that retained the Champions League title remains intact, Les Parisiens have replaced most of the supporting cast. All of Gonçalo Ramos, Lee Kang-in, Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have moved on, amounting to over €300m (£258m) in sales. Torres, Maghnes Akliouche and Mika Godts make up the reigning champions’ new frontline depth options, with Digne being the other senior arrival.

“Those players were important in our quest for trophies, but we needed new energy in the team,” Luis Enrique said.

For the head coach, the toughest departure to make up for will be Bradley Barcola’s. The French international’s move, Luis Enrique explained, was a “special case”, given that he “grew a lot and helped the team grow” during his three years in the capital.

View image in fullscreen Mika Godts joined PSG from Ajax this summer. Photograph: Joachim Azouze/PSG/Getty Images

“He wanted to have a greater role in the team, and that’s not something I’m able to guarantee to any player,” the Spaniard said. “He was an important player and a great person, his teammates loved him. It was his decision and we have to accept it, I wish him all the best.”

The prospect of playing under Luis Enrique was seemingly the primary attraction for the summer arrivals, all of whom spoke to the press during Thursday’s open day at the club’s training ground.

“He was like a footballing father to me when I played for him in the national team,” Torres said of his compatriot. “He believed in me and wanted to bring me here, so I want to repay that confidence,” the former Barcelona man added, before stressing that he would be content to play wherever the head coach needed him. “He gives the front three a lot of freedom to move around, which makes things difficult for our opponents.”

“He’s a great coach, so I was happy to hear that he wanted me here,” Godts said. “He likes players who are versatile, and I’m ready to play anywhere, that’s not an issue,” the Belgian winger continued, “I’ll play on the left, on the right, as a No 10, even as a No 9.”

Monaco, although rocked by a chaotic end to the transfer window, are shaping up to be the sternest of PSG’s early-season tests. They are the only team in the league yet to drop points, and saw off Marseille last week with a double from the early-season breakout star Paris Brunner.

As they prepare to take to the brand new Parc des Princes pitch, it would be difficult to imagine a more enticing opponent to mark the rentrée at home for Luis Enrique’s new and old students.

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 14: West Ham
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 11th (NB: this is not necessarily Suzanne Wrack’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 10th

Prospects

West Ham were in big trouble last December, with half the season gone and one win in 11 games. Rehanne Skinner was dismissed and the former Italy forward Rita Guarino came in to steady the ship. There were questions over how much any manager would be able to do without the club giving a bit more support to the women’s setup, but Skinner, fairly or not, had lost the dressing room and heads were down. The impact of Guarino wasn’t instant, a 5-0 defeat by Chelsea was a cruel introduction. It took a little time to rebuild the confidence of the team and get them playing the way she believed they could, but back-to-back wins against Newcastle in the FA Cup and Leicester in the Women’s Super League followed the Chelsea game, before a huge 3-2 win against Brighton and battling draws with Manchester United and London City Lionesses contributed to 14 points from their final 11 WSL games, taking their total to 19.

As players started to depart in the summer, the situation looked bleak. Among the 14 departures were the forward Shekiera Martinez, who joined Tottenham, Katrina Gorry, who decided to take a break from football, and Shelina Zadorsky, who left at the end of her contract before signing for AFC Toronto. Then the signings started to arrive and suddenly the dark clouds were parting.

The Hammers have had a hugely productive and impressive window with 10 signings, including the forwards Kelly Gago, recruited from Everton, and Ebony Salmon, who joined from Aston Villa, the defenders Estelle Cascarino, whose loan was made permanent, and Nadine Riesen and Laia Codina, who joined from Eintracht Frankfurt and Arsenal respectively, and the young English talents Sienna Wareing and Niamh Peacock who signed from Manchester United and Arsenal. Guarino has been backed in this window and West Ham have a real opportunity to make a statement in the WSL.

Off-field picture

West Ham’s relative indifference towards their women’s team has been long known. There has been a steady decline since the departure of the enthusiastic Jack Sullivan as managing director of the women’s team in 2021 – the son of David Sullivan having been handed control of the side at 18. Little is known of how cash strapped the women’s setup is compared with other WSL sides. The club have not published detailed financial figures throughout their time in the WSL, with their most recent Companies House submission saying they are entitled to exemption from audit under section 479A of the Companies Act 2006. According to Football Association figures they were the WSL’s lowest spenders on agents’ fees in the year to February 2026, at £97,000, and one of only two clubs – Manchester United were the other – whose spend was down year on year.

The manager

Guarino was a relative unknown when she arrived in the WSL, having managed only in Italy. In the second half of the season West Ham didn’t quite experience a new manager bounce, but Guarino was able to guide them to another four wins and a 10th-place finish above Liverpool and Leicester. Guarino has impressed. Codina told the BBC of her transfer talks: “I remember having my first conversation with Rita. It was at the beginning of everything. I had my agent next to me and I was like: ‘Wow.’ The feeling that I got in this meeting is what I want in my future; it is what I want for my next steps.”

Star signing

Gago scored 10 goals in 30 games for Everton but was frustrated there, handing in a written transfer request in January. The 27-year-old has praised West Ham, saying: “The family feel of the club really appealed to me and I’m excited to join that family. I’m going to give everything in order to help the team reach our ambitions and I’m really looking forward to getting started.”

Stat attack

West Ham were the most direct team last season. They moved the ball upfield quicker than anyone and only Leicester averaged fewer passes per possession sequence. There is no right way to play; everyone needs a style. But after West Ham collected fewer points than in three of the preceding four campaigns, is it time for a change of approach?

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Set for a breakthrough

Inès Belloumou played 18 times for West Ham last season after a long wait following her recruitment from Bayern Munich in July 2024. She was sent out on loan straight away, first to Lazio then to Malmö to build up the points to meet the governing body endorsement criteria for international player visas. This summer the 25-year-old, who was born in France and represented the country up to under-23 level before switching allegiance to Algeria, shone at the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations. Named in the team of the tournament, Belloumou started all six Algeria games as they finished third, with the full-back scoring the winning penalty in the shootout at the end of the third-place playoff. Full of confidence, she is ready to kick on in the WSL.

View image in fullscreen Full-back Inès Belloumou crunches into a challenge with Arsenal’s Smilla Holmberg. Photograph: Pedro Porru/MB Media/Getty Images

What they say

“I want to put the club in the highest position in the table and go as far as we can in the cups. For me, the WSL is the best league in the world at the moment and anything can happen. Anything is possible. We need to have a lot of consistency, which is not easy, but it’s why we work hard every day” – Viviane Asseyi, after signing a new contract

Where are they playing their home games?

If you spend too much time dwelling on this you’ll feel as if you’re in Waiting for Godot. The team have not played at the club’s main stadium since a 2-0 loss to Tottenham in front of close to 25,000 fans in September 2019. There has been talk since of it being a priority, including from Skinner, but every year another season ticks on without the team playing at the club’s main home. Instead, the team continue to call Dagenham and Redbridge’s Victoria Road stadium home.

Sports.title: London City claim sponsor deal is record and bigger than some in Premier League
Sports.content:
The Women’s Super League club London City Lionesses’ new front-of-shirt sponsorship deal with Nike is the largest in the women’s game, according to their American owner, Michele Kang.

The length and value of the deal has not been disclosed but sources close to the WSL club are hailing it as a gamechanging moment and Kang claims that it even exceeds some men’s Premier League clubs’ shirt deals.

London City, who host Manchester United on Friday in the opening game of the new WSL campaign, are about to embark on only their second top-flight season, but this summer they have shocked the sport by signing a flurry of some of the biggest names in women’s football, including the former Ballon d’Or winner Alexia Putellas, the former England goalkeeper Mary Earps and Putellas’ Spain and Barcelona teammate, Mapi León.

It has been reported that the largest current front-of-shirt sponsorship deal for a women’s football team is an approximately $4m per year agreement reached by the new NWSL franchise in Atlanta – who will begin competing in 2028, but Kang told BBC Sport: “I can absolutely confirm that this is the largest women-only front-of-shirt deal. It is higher than the Atlanta number.

“I can absolutely also share that it is higher than some of the men’s Premier League front-of-shirt deals. It’s huge. That’s why it is landmark. There are so many other people who believe in the future of women’s football. They [Nike] didn’t make this decision lightly. They did not write a charity cheque. They believe in the future and they believe together we will invest and build this future together.”

View image in fullscreen Michele Kang has been London City Lionesses owner since December 2023. Photograph: Charlotte Wilson/Offside/Getty Images

The deal will be a major boost to London City’s finances. In their most recent set of financial accounts, they posted an annual revenue of just £902,000 for the 2024-25 season, when they won promotion to the top flight. Their operating loss was over £10m, and more than 10 times that revenue.

Their transfer business has attracted questions about how they can fit their lavish spending within the salary cap, as the WSL’s rules dictate that clubs cannot spend more on their player wage bills than 80% of their relevant revenue plus up to £4m of owner contributions. But it is understood this Nike deal will transform their annual revenue astronomically compared to previous seasons.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The popularity on social media of their biggest new signing Alexia Putellas – who has 3.4 million Instagram followers – and Earps and León is believed to have been a major driving factor in the supposedly high valuation from Nike. Putellas has helped Spain win 2023’s World Cup and won the Champions League four times with Barcelona. The Spaniard shared the news of the sponsorship on her Instagram account on Thursday.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford goes under the needle for new Man United tattoo - after winning a place back at his boyhood club when Barcelona rejected him
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford has shown off a new Manchester United tattoo after it became clear he would be staying at the club this season.

The winger, who spent time on loan at Aston Villa and Barcelona over the last two years – not starting for the Red Devils in 626 days until last week – didn't leave in the summer transfer window.

Before he lined up in Michael Carrick's starting XI for the 5-2 win over Ipswich Town on Sunday, it was announced that the England star would wear the No9 shirt – and that has now been reflected in Rashford's latest tattoo.

The 28-year-old gave fans a glimpse at his abdominal tattoo, which features the five shirt numbers he has worn throughout his career.

The numbers ten, 19, and 39, which he previously wore at the club, were already on his stomach, with the No14 he wore at Barcelona last season also added.

Rashford also wore nine at Villa, meaning he has killed two birds with one stone with the new ink.

Marcus Rashford has shown off his new Manchester United tattoo after he remained at the club in the summer

The forward has his career shirt numbers tattooed onto his abdominals and has added to the collection

Celebrity tattoo artist Dale McGovern shared a video showing the process of the art work

The shirts and their numbers are tattooed below the words: 'What your eyes see can be misleading, never judge a book by its cover'.

Upon sharing the snap, Rashford wrote in the caption: 'New number, Same mission…'

He also had a new neck tattoo done, which reads: 'Love and let be.'

The process was carried out by celebrity tattooist Dale McGovern, who has also worked with the likes of influencer Molly Smith, Leeds defender Jayden Bogle, and Rashford's team-mate Ayden Heaven.

Rashford will hope to now settle at United after it had previously looked as though there was no way back for him at the club.

After coming off the bench in the opening day defeat by Hull, Rashford started against Ipswich and provides a more than handy wing option for Michael Carrick.

Defender Harry Maguire, meanwhile, believes a 'happy, driven and hungry' Rashford can be an enormous asset to Manchester United this season.

Barcelona turned down the chance to make Rashford's loan permanent this summer and he returned to Manchester with questions swirling about whether he could be reintegrated into the squad.

He also had a new neck tattoo done by the same artist, which reads: 'Love and let be'

Against Ipswich, he started for United for the first time in 626 days, going all the way back to 2024, and Maguire is convinced that, if Rashford 'wants to work and wants to improve', the sky is the limit again in a United shirt.

'It's been really good since he came in,' Maguire said following the 5-2 win on Sunday.

'He's trained really well and us as players, if Marcus wants to be here and wants to work and wants to improve and wants to help the team, of course, we're willing to have him in the squad.

'He's a great talent. You've seen that he's always a threat. I think today, I think he was a threat constantly, and I think he could still do a lot more and I think he'll say that he can do more.

'I think if we keep him fit, we keep him happy, he keeps driven, keeps hungry, and I think he is a great asset to have.'

Sports.title: Liverpool complete £4.3m move for 18-year-old French forward Djylian N'Guessan - with teenager set to spend the season out on loan
Sports.content:
Liverpool complete £4.3m move for 18-year-old French forward Djylian N'Guessan - with teenager set to spend the season out on loan

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Liverpool have signed talented French forward Djylian N'Guessan on a pre-contract agreement from Saint-Etienne.

The 18-year-old France youth international will spend the the season on loan at Stade Brest in Ligue 1 having signed from the second-tier club.

Liverpool will pay around £4.3million for the youngster who is set to join up with the squad in January, though his situation will be reviewed at the turn of the year with another loan possible.

N'Guessan was spotted playing in the Under-17 Euros in Albania where he was named in the team of the tournament.

His signature represents another coup for Liverpool under the leadership of head of global talent Matt Newberry.

The Reds have signed a number of youngsters in recent years, such as Ifeanyi Ndukwe, Mor Talla Ndiaye, Armin Pesci, Samuel Martinez and Lucca Brughmans.

Liverpool have completed the £4.3m signing of France youth international Djylian N'Guessan

In the first team, they worked to bring in the likes of Bradley Barcola, Victor Munoz and Jeremy Jacquet.

The Reds are back in action this evening when they take on Ipswich at Portman Road in their hunt for the first win of the new season.

Sports.title: Now the MANAGERS are playing minigames! Former Premier League star is challenged to see how many Michael Jackson songs he can fit into a press conference... so did you get them all?
Sports.content:
The football minigames that have become a phenomenon thanks to former Premier League referee Mike Dean seem to have made their way into management – in a more light-hearted way.

Former Newcastle and England midfielder and current Southend United manager Kieron Dyer came clean during his pre-match press conference ahead of his side's fifth-tier game against Yeovil Town that he had been put up to a challenge by members of his squad.

As Dyer's press conference came to a close, members of the media got up to leave the room, before Dyer grabbed their attention to make his confession.

'Sorry, sorry, just to say...' Dyer began. 'I was challenged by the lads to see how many Michael Jackson songs I could get into my press conference. The money will be donated to charity, but I got quite a few in, I think.'

Those in the room were left stunned, as they playfully questioned how the 33-cap ex-England star had managed the feat.

Southend shared a clip of all of Dyer's references to their social media pages. Some were more smooth than others, including the first: 'Obviously at the club we want to be starting something really good, and recruitment is a massive part of that,' was said in reference to Jackson's 1983 hit Wanna Be Startin' Somethin'.

🕺 A bit of a recurring theme in today’s press conference.. https://t.co/RfeeTB25jJ pic.twitter.com/sFbiTAmSAU — Southend United FC (@SUFCRootsHall) September 3, 2026

Kieron Dyer was challenged by his Southend players to fit Michael Jackson song names into his press conference

Others, though, felt more forced. Dyer added: 'I expect a real thriller of a game on Saturday,' and: 'It's always good to reflect and look at the man in the mirror.'

Perhaps the most impressive inclusion was when he got two Jackson songs into one sentence, saying: 'Football is never going to be black or white, there's going to be the good and the bad,' in reference to 1991 and 1987 hits Black or White and Bad.

Later, when talking about transfers, he continued: 'We have targets in mind. I can't name names, but it could be a random Joe Bloggs or a random Billie Jean.'

No one in the press room seemed to pick up on the references, and a laughing Dyer said after the press conference had ended: 'I can't believe you didn't clock that. Especially when I said Billie Jean.

'Sorry about that, but I got challenged and hopefully I've raised some money for charity.'

The press conference came a matter of hours after former Premier League official Dean came under fire for supposedly admitting to playing his own minigames during top flight matches.

Dean, 58, retired from refereeing in 2023 after over 20 years of officiating at the highest level in English football.

Now that the dust has settled on his professional career in the game, Dean has admitted to playing a game where he would see how long he could go without blowing his whistle during Premier League matches.

Mike Dean has admitted to sometimes trying to see how long he could go without blowing his whistle when refereeing Premier League matches

The ex-official also revealed that he would try and stay in the centre circle for as long as he could during some games.

'There used to be games we would have for a laugh,' Dean said on Jamie Vardy's Having a Party podcast. 'It would kick-off, right; see how long we could go without blowing a whistle.

'I done that a few times in the Premier League, before VAR, obviously. Went 20, 25 minutes without blowing the whistle.'

Dean continued: 'I used to do another one in the Premier League, I used to stand in the centre circle and see how long I could stay in the centre circle before I had to leave. That was just me joking about. Got about 15 minutes once, in one game.'

Daily Mail Sport understands his comments have raised eyebrows within the refereeing community, with senior figures questioning the plausibility of his claim given the lack of detail.

According to senior officials, Dean provided no indication of when the alleged minigames took place. He also claimed they occurred before VAR was introduced for the 2019-20 season, meaning any such incidents would have taken place under previous refereeing chiefs – and current bosses are insistent that 'integrity and impartiality' are at the heart of referees' decision-making.

Sports.title: Roy Keane goes viral after leaving Gary Neville and Co in stitches with hilarious comparison between football stat and 'speaking to girls in a nightclub'
Sports.content:
Roy Keane goes viral after leaving Gary Neville and Co in stitches with hilarious comparison between football stat and 'speaking to girls in a nightclub'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Roy Keane left his Stick to Football colleagues in fits of laughter following his thoughts about the statistic 'Expected Goals' (xG).

Speaking on the latest episode of the show, brought to you by Disney+, the former Manchester United captain expressed why he believes that particular stat - which measures the probability that a given shot will result in a goal - is irrelevant.

Sitting alongside Gary Neville, Jamie Carragher, Jill Scott and Ian Wright, Keane started his point animatedly with: 'Do you know what that stat is?

'Years ago, when you'd go to a nightclub back in the day, and you'd chat to a girl all night, but you go home by yourself. What's your xG?'

Keane's quip left Neville, Carragher, Scott and Wright in stitches. Neville then replied self-depreciatingly: 'Roy, I kept clean sheets!'

A smirking Roy said: 'I'm sure you did, yeah!'

xG explained the Roy Keane way! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/qJOS705noc — The Overlap (@WeAreTheOverlap) September 3, 2026

Roy Keane left his Stick to Football colleagues laughing with his views on Expected Goals (xG)

Gary Neville (left) and Jamie Carragher were in hysterics after Keane compared it to nightclubs

During the show, the quintet discussed the closing of the summer transfer window - following Tuesday's 11pm deadline.

Among the clubs discussed was Liverpool - with Carragher believing Reds boss Andoni Iraola needs to have an awkward conversation with his vice-captain Dominik Szoboszlai and move him to right back permanently.

Szoboszlai, 25, was rewarded with a new £350,000-a-week contract this summer after being named Liverpool’s Player of the Season for his impressive performances in midfield last campaign - one of the few positives in what was otherwise a disappointing season for the Reds under Arne Slot.

Despite establishing himself as a mainstay in midfield, the Hungarian has also been called upon to deputise at right-back, doing so sporadically last season and again during the second half of Liverpool’s 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest on Saturday.

Carragher believes Szoboszlai may be tasked with the right-back role permanently after Liverpool's disjointed start under Iraola, who has drawn both his Premier League matches so far.

With Conor Bradley still injured and Jeremie Frimpong struggling for form, right-back has become a problem position for Liverpool since Trent Alexander-Arnold's exit to Real Madrid last summer.

Fearing it was a 'massive mistake' not to bolster Liverpool's ranks at full back in the transfer window, Carragher is confident Szoboszlai could provide a solution for Iraola.

Carragher believes Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola (right) needs to have an awkward conversation with his vice-captain Dominik Szoboszlai (left) and move him to right-back

'The big thing he (Iraola) has got, and it happened last season and at the weekend, Szoboszlai went back to right-back. I've never believed Szoboszlai is a central midfield player,' Carragher said.

'Now, he's signed a new contract and I can only imagine in those talks, they were desperate for him to stay, he's almost said "I want to play midfield". He's moved around a bit and he started the season in central midfield. I don't see him as that.

'For me, in midfield he's a Jordan Henderson. Runner, energy, with more of a goal threat. But Liverpool don't play that way and he's not really a No 10. His best role could actually be at right-back. He'd get plenty of the ball, he can run and almost play that Trent role from there.

'But there's no way he's going to want to play there because he's just signed a new contract for £350,000 a week. You've just done this big thing, he's the vice-captain, I just think that's a conversation Iraola is going to have to have going forward, because the midfield is not right and he's part of that midfield not being right.'

Sports.title: Naomi Osaka calls on US Open influencers to 'read up on tennis etiquette' after umpire was forced to tell off spectators during her first match
Sports.content:
Naomi Osaka calls on US Open influencers to 'read up on tennis etiquette' after umpire was forced to tell off spectators during her first match

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Naomi Osaka called upon influencers travelling to the US Open to 'read up' on the sport's rules for spectators after her first-round match was disrupted by a rowdy group in one of Arthur Ashe Stadium's luxury suites.

The four-time Grand Slam champion had been preparing to serve when the chair umpire told off the guests for appearing to stage an impromptu photoshoot, complete with portable lights.

'Guys, please, in the suite behind me, please thank you guys, please take your seat,' the chair umpire announced to the stadium, as the broadcast camera panned to a group milling freely within their prime seats, taking pictures and talking.

While Osaka was only half-focused on the specifics of the incident while immersed in defeating her opponent Anastasia Zakharova, discussing what happened on the tournament's showcourt two days later, she suggested that more could be done to ensure that players were not disturbed during matchplay.

'I think obviously, if you come to a sporting event, you have to respect the sport,' she said after her defeat of Katerina Siniakova, which took place on the same court. 'And I feel like it's common courtesy to read up on the sport, especially the etiquette.

'I feel like it could be a good thing for people to make the sport of tennis popular to their specific audience, but I think it has to be managed a lot better, especially in the situation like first-round match.

Naomi Osaka called for fans new to tennis to learn the sport's etiquette after her match was disrupted by influencers

'Overall I think there is huge positives,' she added, on the topic of influencers more generally. 'You want people to continue to grow the sport. I just think it has to be in a way that everyone knows the rules and the etiquette.'

Etiquette largely dictates that fans should save conversation and movement for changeovers or set breaks, when the players are at the chairs. But in 2024, the US Open switched to a policy of 'free fan movement', which allows spectators to move during points regardless of on-court action.

Of the incident itself, Osaka said that she had been more bothered by the noise inside the stadium during both her matches - a constant chatter which complements the endless movement - than the flash lights themselves.

'I was going to say today the umpire, she told everyone to be quiet more than I've ever heard an umpire tell a crowd to be quiet,' she continued.

'I do think in my first match, I wasn't really paying attention. I tell people I normally just focus on the match and the court, but there was a moment where there was, like, people shouting, and you could hear it quite clearly. I think it bothered my opponent, too.

'Maybe that's what you were talking about, but I've heard some people say, like, the lights or whatever. I don't really see the lights, because obviously, when you are serving, you're looking at the sun or you're looking at the night lights. It was more the noise.'

Daily Mail Sport contacted the tournament for comment on after Osaka's press conference, with US Open head of communications Brendan McIntyre sharing the following statement: 'The USTA is always striving to grow tennis in this country and bring new audiences into the sport. The US Open is our greatest opportunity to do so, and we welcome newcomers to our event.

'We want all of our fans and guests to have an incredible time when they attend, but we also need to ensure they do not interfere with the action and competition on the court. We are continually looking for ways to ensure fans in the stands know what is permitted and what is prohibited.

'As a result, we have increased signage on the grounds and in stadium, and messaged ticket and suite holders to remind everyone to refrain from any activity that could disrupt the game, including noise levels, flash photography and ring lights. The chair umpire also has the ability to address the crowd if and when necessary.'

READ MORE - How influencers are killing the US Open and turning it into a 'zoo': Angry top stars hit out at 'disrespectful' and noisy content creators disrupting matches for pictures

Sports.title: Aussie tennis firebrand Nick Kyrgios enters rehab after testing positive for cocaine use
Sports.content:
Fallen Australian tennis star Nick Kyrgios has entered a treatment program after accepting a one-month ban for testing positive for cocaine.

After admitting his 'huge mistake' when initially suspended for failing a drugs test on June 22 at an ATP 250 tournament in Spain, Kyrgios is allowed to compete again from Friday.

Kyrgios, who had been provisionally suspended since August 4, had faced a ban ranging from a baseline three-month period to up to four years.

During an interview with investigators from the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA), Kyrgios explained his use of cocaine had occurred socially during a night out, days before he was due to play in Mallorca.

The ITIA consulted an independent scientific expert at a World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)-accredited laboratory, who stated the explanation was consistent with the level of cocaine found in his sample.

As a result, the ITIA accepted Kyrgios's use of cocaine was outside of competition.

Nick Kyrgios said he had used cocaine socially, and the ITIA accepted his use was out of competition

Kyrgios has apologised to his fans and sponsors after failing a drug test

Under WADA rules, the default suspension for a breach of this type is three months, which can be further reduced to one month if the individual commits to a treatment program approved by the ITIA.

The 2022 Wimbledon finalist also forfeited the €6,570 (roughly $10,607) he won in Mallorca for losing in the first round to countryman Adam Walton.

But his suspension was reduced for agreeing to enter a treatment program.

The ITIA said Kyrgios, whose career world ranking peaked at number 13, could appeal against the provisional suspension but he opted against doing so.

'I recently failed a drug test in Mallorca after testing positive for cocaine,' Kyrgios posted on Instagram last month.

'I made a huge mistake and I take full responsibility for it. I'm sorry to my fans, my family, my sponsors and everyone close to me.

'Above all, I'm sorry to the kids who follow me. I know the example this sets and I'm deeply disappointed in myself.'

Kyrgios, who played only four official singles matches on the elite ATP Tour this year, has battled knee and wrist injuries in recent years and has all but conceded he is finished as a singles force.

Kyrgios has promised to come back better after the suspension was handed down

'I'm not going to make excuses, but I do want to give some context about where I've been,' Kyrgios wrote.

'The last couple of years of injuries have taken a huge toll on me, both physically and mentally.

'My body hasn't been able to do what my mind expects it to do, and coming to terms with being near the end of my career has been harder than I ever imagined.'

But the polarising Canberra-born drawcard said that didn't excuse his actions.

'I've always said I didn't choose tennis - tennis chose me,' he wrote.

'But letting go of something that has been my whole life is one of the hardest things I've ever had to face. At times I've felt helpless and alone. None of that excuses what I did.'

Kyrgios said 'the good news is that this has given me a wake up call.

'For the next 28 days, I'll be stepping away from social media and public life while I focus on getting myself right.

'I'd ask that people respect my privacy during that time, and most importantly the privacy of my family. I'm sorry. I'll do the work and come back better.'

The ITIA said Kyrgios was suspended for a ‌positive test for benzoylecgonine, a cocaine metabolite, with a WADA laboratory confirming the positive result on July 17.

The 31-year-old was banned from playing, coaching or attending any tournaments sanctioned by the men's and women's tennis tours worldwide and national-level events in Australia.

Kyrgios last played in the men's doubles at Wimbledon in London on July 2, when he and partner Alexander Bublik lost in the first round.

Sports.title: Last British star standing at the US Open Francesca Jones is downed by teen talent Iva Jovic - as all nine players fail to make the third round
Sports.content:
Britain's singles hopes at the US Open officially ended on Thursday evening, as Francesca Jones was knocked out in a gritty battle against rising American talent Iva Jovic, 6-4, 6-4.

Jones was the last Briton standing by virtue of the scheduling, the final match on Court 17 - the so-called 'weed court' - where she has previously played a number of qualifying matches. And in the first set, Jones put up more than enough fight to spare the blushes of her compatriots in the second round of the women's draw, Katie Boulter and Harriet Dart, who managed just five games between them in their straight-sets losses.

When Jovic grabbed the opening break, Jones' support may have feared the worst. The 18-year-old is already the 14th seed in Flushing Meadows, and has a fluid game style built on soaking up pressure and firing back bullets that may one day see her snap up the No1 seeding here.

After a run of three games, Jones stopped the rot with a break of Jovic's serve, and the match really began.

Jones is nothing if not a fighter. Describing how 'Northern grit' got her over the line in her stop-start, weather-disturbed win against Magda Linette, that was on full display here as she grew into the game in front of a partisan home crowd, her feel for the ball improving quickly in the early stages.

Jovic was put under pressure even in the games she won, with Jones frequently dogging her to deuce and keeping her foot on her opponent's serve. The opening set stretched to 56 minutes. Just three minutes shy of Boulter's entire star-crossed match against Karolina Muchova on Thursday.

Francesca Jones was unable to get past rising American star Iva Jovic on a tough evening

The 18-year-old is the 14th seed in Flushing Meadows but did not have an easy time against the British qualifier

The 25-year-old was able to hang tough in the rallies as she threw the book at Jovic, a variety of backhand slices splintering cross-court, deeply struck forehands, and the occasional net rush.

But there was a mental game to be played here. 'Confidence, it's all about confidence,' Jones' coach told her in Spanish, almost a mother tongue since her move to Barcelona to train at the age of nine. With Jovic reaching deuce looking to pull off yet another break for 5-3, Jones listened, knuckled down, and pulled off the all-important hold.

When Jovic's class told to hand her the opening set, it looked for a moment as if Jones' race was run. Four games on the run were gobbled up by Jovic, her spot in the third round almost in touching distance. But the Briton stayed cool, and continued to construct her points well. Suddenly, she had three break-point opportunities. One and two came and went, but as Jones wafted a sky-high moonball over to Jovic, she blinked, and fumbled her shot into the net. Finally, a game on the board. All about confidence? Jones sent some racquets off for re-stringing. That can take about 20 minutes. She was digging in.

As in the first set, Jovic looked to wrestle momentum back at 4-2. Again, Jones was in no mood to roll over. A wicked backhand ladened with unpredictable spin was too much for Jovic, and pulled back one break point, and three deuces eventually handed the hold to Jones a second time.

But Jovic chose a good time to serve well, and fast. For the first time since the very start of the match, the teenager was efficient in her hold. The conditions were steamy even as the clock ticked towards 9pm, and off-court relief beckoned. But as she looked to break Jones, her rival's dangerous slice again held back the tide, mulching two match-point opportunities for Jovic and allowing her to carry off a gutsy hold. With sweat pouring off both of the players, ball kids used the break to mop the court.

Jovic would have to do it on her own racquet, and with nerveless cool, shrugged off the late drama of a missed net cord to serve out the match. Her win in straight sets undersells how hard she had to fight against a player in Jones who won her first ever US Open main draw match on Wednesday.

British No2 - and onetime world No8 - Cameron Norrie was the first Briton with direct entry into the main draw to fall on the opening day's play, with defeat to French 22-year-old Luca van Assche.

Other first-round casualties included Arthur Fery, who lost in straight sets to Lorenzo Musetti, and Jan Choinski, who was despatched by the same scoreline to Botic van de Zandschulp. Qualifier Harry Wendelken was unable to see his strong form which gained him entry into the tournament proper translate against the No21 seed Luciano Darderi.

But fellow qualifiers Toby Samuel and Jacob Fearnley fared a little better, reaching the second round. Samuel put in a particularly bold performance against Tomas Machac, feasting on the inconsistent Czech to take him in straight sets. Fearnley meanwhile qualified as a lucky loser, and proved why he deserved his spot with an extended, heavily rain-delayed first-round victory against Martin Landaluce.

Both however fell in the second-round, with Samuel another victim of a challenging draw against Jiri Lehecka, and Fearnley leaving a fightback in the third set too late to make it stick against Tomas Martin Etcheverry. All three British women in the draw, Dart, Jones, and Boulter, made it to the second round.

Sports.title: Why Roberto De Zerbi still thinks he can get the best out of 'future Ballon d'Or winner' Mykhailo Mudryk at Tottenham, from their Shakhtar secrets to the 'hope' of Spurs' forward line
Sports.content:
Tottenham's latest great hope is that Roberto De Zerbi will work some magic on Mykhailo Mudryk.

De Zerbi once hailed Mudryk as a future Ballon D'Or winner and sure enough the footage from a time when he was Brighton boss has resurfaced since the pair were reunited at Spurs on transfer deadline day.

They worked together at Shakhtar Donetsk, so De Zerbi has a good appreciation of the 25-year-old Ukraine who has joined him on loan for the season with a £75million option to buy.

He knows the depth of the winger's talent, his footballing strengths and weaknesses, his personality and attitude.

Unfortunately, much has gone awry for Mudryk since leaving Shakhtar.

His £89m move to Chelsea already looked like a flop when the doping ban hit in November 2024.

Mykhailo Mudryk has not played since November 2024, serving a year and a half of his four-year doping ban before it was cut short this summer

Mudryk and Roberto De Zerbi have reunited at Tottenham having worked together at Shakhtar Donetsk in the Ukraine

Now, two years after his last Premier League start, De Zerbi has set about the task of rekindling this talent and replenishing his morale in the hope it might solve a problem for Spurs.

It seems like a longshot and yet Mudryk is not the only great hope in play in N17.

Everyone hopes Dejan Kulusevski is nearing the end of his injury nightmare and will soon be back in contention. The same can be said for James Maddison and Mohamed Kudus, two of the most creative players at Spurs who hardly kicked a ball in 2026.

And for Dominic Solanke, whose last season was disrupted by injuries and who has missed part of pre-season with more niggling and unexplained issues.

Savio and Omar Marmoush have been lured from Manchester City's bench in the hope they might recapture form they showed before moving to English football.

Mathys Tel remains an enigma 20 months after his arrival from Bayern Munich but is only 21, still young, a work in progress and everyone hopes he can fulfil his vast potential.

De Zerbi's entire strike-force is built on hope.

Last night, Spurs confirmed their 25-man squad for the Premier League did not include Richarlison, the storm-tossed Brazilian now angling after a move to Trabzonspor before the Turkish transfer deadline on Friday.

Mudryk won player of the season in his one year under De Zerbi in 2021-22

His form for Shakhtar earned him his £89m move to Chelsea in January 2023

Richarlison was the top scorer for Spurs last season, and for all his faults, his omission leaves the attacking unit dangerously low on game time in recent months.

Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert are in the squad but weeks from fitness after serious knee injuries earlier this year and the other eight attacking or creative players total only 33 appearances and nine goals in the league this year.

There is never any such thing as a guarantee, but it feels like De Zerbi is taking off into the new season on a wing and a prayer when it comes to goals and an attacking threat.

Goals have been a problem ever since Ange Postecoglou's lust for thrills was replaced by Thomas Frank's caution and defensive security which cost the team fluency and sparked an over-reliance on goals from set pieces.

Since Frank was sacked, the threat from set pieces has faded and Spurs sold or released many of their strongest players in the air. Cristian Romero, Kevin Danso, Radu Dragusin, Joao Palhinha and Randal Kolo Muani have all departed.

Brentford tormented Spurs in the air on the opening day of the season. Others will take note.

Spurs' defensive upgrade made sense. It was complete in good time, early in the summer and injected much-needed leadership, experience and proven Premier League quality into the squad.

Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes were expensive and are yet to find their best rhythm but should strengthen midfield.

Questions linger about Toni Kinsky as the number one goalkeeper, but when Cody Gakpo and Iliman Ndiaye escaped Spurs, it left uncertainty swirling around firepower.

De Zerbi's team are one of three Premier League teams without a goal from the opening two games.

Mudryk's career is at a crossroads and he desperately needs to revive his fortunes at Spurs

Still, there's always hope.

Marmoush was red hot for 18 months at Eintracht Frankfurt. Savio had that good year at Girona and dazzled on his debut against Charlton's reserves in the Carabao Cup only to miss the Newcastle defeat because Spurs physios detected muscle fatigue.

This is always a concern for those who are not conditioned by the rigours of regular competitive football.

Nobody expects Kulusevski will return in the same sublime form he was in under Postecoglou two years ago. Nobody would be surprised if he encountered a physical setback or two as he returned.

The same is true for Maddison, who for various reasons has not started a game for even longer than Kulusevski. And for Kudus, who has not started a game since January.

Mudryk has not been injured but has been out for the longest of all.

The relationship at Shakhtar counts for something, but it is a very tall order to expect De Zerbi to bring him back to the boil instantly.

Much of the excitement about Mudryk's potential resides in a six-week spell when he scored eight in 10 games for Shakhtar, a flurry that sparked a rush for his signature, led by Arsenal for a long time and won by Chelsea who gave him an eight-and-a-half-year contract.

De Zerbi had left Ukraine by this stage. Having arrived at Shakhtar at the start of the season which never returned from its winter break because of Russia invading in February 2022, the Italian quit and was out of work until Brighton appointed him in September 2022.

He did give Mudryk his big break however, and the young winger responded.

Enzo Maresca was in charge of Chelsea when Mudryk returned the positive result for banned the substance meldonium in October 2024

'I know the value of Mudryk,' said De Zerbi when Brighton boss and Premier League clubs were chasing the Shakhtar winger. 'He can win the Ballon D'Or in future. He has the quality to become a star.'

Mudryk's exhilarating speed is his key asset, and he delivered many of his most exciting Shakhtar performances in the surreal environment of wartime football played at neutral venues behind closed doors.

Upon joining Chelsea in January 2023, he went 10 months without a goal.

He flickered without convincing amid the managerial whirl at Stamford Bridge from Graham Potter to Frank Lampard to Mauricio Pochettino and Enzo Maresca, who was in charge when he returned the positive result for the banned substance meldonium during an out-of-competition test while training with Ukraine in October 2024.

None of them denied he had genuine talent. None though could translate it to the Premier League.

By the time of the ban, Mudryk was firmly on the outskirts of Maresca's team. His last three Chelsea goals were scored in the early rounds of what became a procession to the Europa Conference League.

In the Premier League under Maresca, he had been reduced to the role of a late substitute whose extreme pace might cause problems for tired defenders when the game was stretched open and misshapen near the end.

So, there is more to rehabilitating Mudryk than simply making up for time missed, he must also reach a level that seemed beyond him before the ban.

If he has an impact at Spurs it will be for the first time in English football and it will one way or another benefit their bitter London rivals Chelsea.

Perhaps it is a sign of De Zerbi's desperation that he thinks it is worth a shot.

At least, with no European competition there is the time to work on the training pitch, drilling shape and searching of his best formula and should not need to overload those who are so short of competitive football.

Fingers crossed Spurs fans.

Sports.title: Ex-Chelsea star Alexandre Pato has takeover deal approved as EFL club release statement
Sports.content:
Ex-Chelsea star Alexandre Pato has takeover deal approved as EFL club release statement

Former Chelsea star Alexandre Pato is in talks to take over a struggling League Two side as he returns to English football

View 2 Images Former Chelsea star Alexandre Pato is in talks to take over at Northampton Town (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

Former Chelsea, AC Milan and Brazil forward Alexandre Pato has had a takeover deal approved for League Two side Northampton Town. The Cobblers have released a statement to say Sports Alpha Capital (SAC), a consortium which includes the 37-year-old, has had a " proposed shareholding acquisition" of the club approved by the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) and English Football League (EFL).

‌



The exact size of SAC's proposed shareholding has not been disclosed at this stage, but the takeover comes just a few months after pulling out of a takeover with League Two side Colchester United. Northampton say the exact details of the investment will be disclosed at a later stage when the deal is completed.

‌



The London-based independent investment management firm Gemcorp Capital are also listed as one of the investors making up the SAC consortium. Pato retired from professional football three years ago and is on the verge of taking the next step in his football career with the bid to take over the troubled Cobblers.

‌



8 controversial Mike Dean moments from row with Arsenal manager to celebrating goal READ MORE :

Colchester United issue statement after John Terry takeover reports READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Northampton chairman Kelvin Thomas said: "This has been a detailed and rigorous process, involving significant scrutiny of the proposed investment, the ownership structure, financial sustainability, and the suitability and financial standing of those involved.

"The successful completion of both the IFR and EFL processes represents an important milestone for the club and should provide supporters and stakeholders with further confidence in the proposed investment and the foundations being put in place for the club's future.

‌



"We would like to thank both the EFL and the IFR for their professionalism, diligence and thoroughness throughout their respective processes.

"As supporters will see from their varied backgrounds, there is a genuine passion for football within the group. A number of the investors have already visited Northampton, spent time at the club and attended matches.

View 2 Images Alexandre Pato is best known for his time at AC Milan but played in the Premier League for Chelsea (Image: Claudio Villa/Getty Images)

‌



"They will bring a strong blend of football, corporate and financial expertise to the club and with significant Brazilian representation within the group we also hope they might bring a little Brazilian excitement and flair with them.

"Now the regulatory processes have been completed we move towards completing the remaining documentation and finalising the investment. Full details regarding the investment, structure and the principal investors involved will be announced upon completion.

"We thank the fans for their patience, but it is reassuring that these in-depth processes are in place for football." Northampton finished bottom of League One last season and were relegated to the fourth-tier of English football and find themselves without a win in 2026-27.

Article continues below

Pato won 27 caps for Brazil and is best known in Europe for his six years with AC Milan, where he won Serie A in 2010/11. He also played for Brazilian sides Internacional, Corinthians and Sao Paulo, as well as Villarreal, Orlando City and Chelsea, where he spent a brief loan spell in 2016.

Sports.title: Katie Taylor bows out of boxing with claim to go down as greatest female fighter of all time
Sports.content:
Katie Taylor bows out of boxing with claim to go down as greatest female fighter of all time

Katie Taylor will bring the curtain down on a stunning boxing career when she fights Flora Pili at Croke Park this weekend - she is already in a league of her own regardless of the outcome

View 2 Images Katie Taylor will box for the final time at Croke Park this weekend (Image: Al Bello/Getty Images for Netflix)

Muhammad Ali fought Al Blue Lewis at Croke Park before a crowd of 18,000 in 1972. Compare that to the 80,000-plus who will cheer Katie Taylor into retirement.

‌



Ali was at the height of his fame, the greatest athlete of the 20th Century. Taylor has a decent claim to be the greatest female boxer that has ever lived. Clarissa Shields is also amazing, but it is not only about fighting. It’s about how you carry yourself. Above all, Taylor is a lovely human being, kind, generous and utterly without self regard.

‌



I remember screaming my head off for her at the 2012 Olympics in London. That was a game changer for female boxing, the first time women had taken part at the Olympics.

‌



Taylor was magnificent in taking gold and has continued that in the pro game. She pioneered the professional age, and that is not to forget those who came before.

Moses Itauma has stunning claim debunked after Filip Hrgovic loss READ MORE :

The likes of Jane Couch in the UK, and Christy Martin in the USA broke the ground, but it was Taylor and the first wave of Olympians who carried the torch forward, legitimising females in the ring in a way that was not possible before.

Taylor never had destructive power. It was her speed and technique that did the damage, stepping in and out of range and overwhelming opponents with rapid combinations. You have only to look at her face to see how good she was. She leaves with barely a mark on her, which is remarkable.

‌



Many of those in attendance on Saturday will not be fans of boxing necessarily but want to be part of history. As well as laying claim to being the best female fighter ever she might also be Ireland’s greatest sports person.

There have been some world class performers, greats like athlete Sonia O’Sullivan, footballer Roy Keane, rugby star Brian O’Driscoll, jockey Ruby Walsh etc, but this girl won everything and did so breaking the mould for women.

View 2 Images Taylor will bow out following her fight with Flora Pili (Image: Brian Lawless/PA Wire)

‌



I admire her so much. Despite her fame she is so humble and encouraging of others. She never talks about herself as a great champion. She lets others decide, which is refreshing when you hear the way the majority of modern fighters go at it.

Everything that is good about boxing is represented by her. She is an inspiration to a generation of young girls coming through, and a fantastic ambassador.

In retirement I would advise her to keep busy in the gym but not boxing. When I stopped I never hit the bags or the pads again. I didn’t want the temptation. Neither, I hope, will she.
