World.title: Teacher says winning teens' attention is a daily battle in literature class
World.content:
Writer and Tabasalu High School literature teacher Jürgen Rooste says that teaching is often a daily struggle for students' attention, but some encounters and moments also give a great deal of energy.

Rooste began working at Tabasalu High School five years ago, when the school opened in 2021. Standing in front of a class is often stressful for him.

"It's a daily fight. When you walk to the front of the class as a teacher, every day is a battle or a war. Some days you come home broken and worn out. That's 90 percent of the days. And then there are some days that are great and give you energy," he said.

According to Rooste, one of a teacher's biggest tasks is to spark interest in students and make them notice what is happening in class. He says literature is not inherently interesting for young people, and teachers must work hard to make it so.

"You face the fact that you have to fight for every moment just to get them to notice anything at all. Some sense of interest or excitement is broken. Literature as such simply isn't interesting. To make literature interesting, you have to fight enormously."

He noted that a teacher must be both demanding and able to find ways to spark curiosity. His own deep love of literature does not mean students automatically share it.

"I'm not the best teacher just because I love literature. I want everyone to be fans of literature, of these texts and things like I am, but of course it doesn't work that way," he admitted.

Tabasalu haridushoones Autor/allikas: Tõnu Tunnel

For teachers, fighting for students' attention has become an everyday issue. This includes phone use. One option, he says, is a rule that phones are not used at all in class unless needed for learning. But that also means the teacher takes responsibility onto themselves.

"If one teacher alone starts banning phones — saying that in my class you can't use them — then there's always the chance you take the hit yourself. I have that option, that choice, but I haven't taken it," he said.

Rooste teaches in upper secondary school, and he believes students at that level should be more capable of being present in their studies. Now he sees attitudes in high school that he previously associated more with basic school.

"I remember that high‑school classes were already a transition phase — they wanted to be more adult, they wanted to be a bit present and show it, not that every moment they could chat with a friend, they would."

Reading checks have not disappeared from his classes. Students can do them with the book and their own notes. The teacher cannot fully control the use of artificial intelligence in note‑taking. "At least it has been digested in some secondary or tertiary form," he said.

When choosing works, he gives students a list of options but also experiments with reading different texts side by side. His literature program also includes younger Estonian authors.

Jürgen Rooste Autor/allikas: Maria Esko

World.title: Iraqi judiciary completes interrogation of 5,700 ISIS suspects
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Supreme Judicial Council of Iraq has officially concluded the interrogation process for 5,704 ISIS detainees who were moved from northeastern Syria earlier this year, preparing them for trial.

The First Karkh Investigation Court said in a statement on Tuesday that it concluded the investigation phase of one of Iraq’s largest terrorism-related cases in history.

The verified detainees originate from 67 different nationalities, including 3,497 Syrians and 474 Iraqis.

The courts identified very dangerous agents in key leadership, military, financial, media, and security roles inside ISIS.

Six offenders were actively linked to the captivity, detention, transfer, sale, and exploitation of Yazidi women, exposing serious international crimes.

Several suspects have previously been cleared and released due to insufficient evidence linking them to terrorism crimes.

In 2014, the terrorist group ISIS took control of large areas in Iraq and Syria before being defeated in 2017.

Over five million Iraqis had to flee the governorates of Nineveh, Salah al-Din, parts of Kirkuk, Diyala, and Anbar because of ISIS control over these areas in 2014.

Although Iraq declared in late 2017 that all of its regions were free of ISIS, the government continues to conduct security operations to hunt out any remaining members of the terrorist group.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate rises in Baghdad, remain stable in Erbil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar rose on Thursday in Baghdad, the Iraqi capital, and remained stable in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,547.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,546.5 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad rose, ranging between 1,552.5 Iraqi dinars and 1,542.5 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate remained stable, fluctuating between 1,546 and 1,545.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation represented more than a 10 percent difference in exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq exports fuel oil through Jordan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told Attaqa News that Iraq began exporting fuel oil shipments via Jordan for the first time last month.

Al-Rikabi explained that Iraq is exporting fuel oil through the neighboring country, not to Jordan.

The Iraqi official did not disclose the details of the agreement, its duration, or when it came into effect.

Iraqi oil shipments started flowing to Jordan in early August through the Trebil border crossing, the only land border crossing between the two countries, at a rate of 10,000 barrels per day, which were stored in the facilities of the Jordan Oil Terminals Company (JOTC), Jordan’s state-owned petroleum logistics and independent storage provider.

Through Jordan, a shipment totaling 307,000 barrels was exported to Greece.

Following the Strait of Hormuz crisis, which began with the United States’ war against Iran on February 28, Iraqi fuel oil shipments began transiting through Syria via tanker trucks, with storage at the Baniyas refinery before shipping to worldwide markets.

Between March and the end of August, Iraq exported 21.4 million barrels of fuel oil through Syria and only 307,000 barrels through Jordan.

Iraqi fuel oil exports started to increase following the Middle East conflict until the end of August in an attempt to compensate for the declining supplies via the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: 38 officers, 3,000 personnel dismissed over corruption in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Interior announced on Thursday that it permanently dismissed 38 officers and 180 personnel over administrative and financial corruption, with another 3,245 personnel discharged for desertion.

The purge represents a significant internal effort as part of the ongoing “Operation Dawn,” a nationwide anti-corruption campaign spearheaded by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government. The campaign has targeted numerous public officials and high-profile individuals.

According to an official statement from Miqdad Miri, the spokesperson for the Interior Ministry, the total number of individuals affected encompasses various categories of misconduct.

After receiving clear evidence of their direct involvement in bribery and financial misconduct, 38 officers were permanently removed from service.

Finalized judicial verdicts convicting 180 enlisted personnel of corruption accusations resulted in their official removal from service.

As part of larger ministry attempts to reestablish strong institutional discipline, 3,245 service personnel were discharged only for abandoning their duties.

These dismissals took place within the first 100 days of the current government’s tenure.

This security-sector cleanup is part of the larger nationwide drive “Operation Dawn.” Between late June and August, security operations resulted in the arrest of at least 210 lawmakers, public servants, and business executives.

World.title: Iraq, AIIB discuss financing development projects
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Finance Minister Faleh Sari met with a delegation from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) led by Konstantin Limitovskiy on Wednesday to discuss funding infrastructure and development projects in Iraq.

During their meeting in Baghdad, the AIIB delegation reviewed its global and regional portfolios to outline how its framework will apply to Iraq across the transportation, energy, water, and digital infrastructure sectors, according to a statement cited by the Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The discussions focused on the Development Road Project, Iraq’s mega-highway and rail corridor intended to connect the Gulf to Europe.

The AIIB publicly stated its willingness to fund and assist this important trans-regional corridor, acknowledging its enormous potential to drive economic diversification.

The Iraqi Ministry of Transport held separate discussions with the World Bank and the AIIB to determine the technological integrations necessary for the project’s ports and rail networks.

The AIIB delegation expressed its willingness to assist and fund important projects in Iraq, particularly major infrastructure projects, such as the Development Road project, which would boost the country’s economic development.

World.title: Iraq launches plan to recover 100,000 artifacts smuggled abroad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has launched a comprehensive plan to recover over 100,000 artifacts that were unearthed through illegal excavation and smuggled out of the country.

The Iraqi Ministry of Culture, Tourism, and Antiquities announced a broad endeavor to recover the country’s stolen Mesopotamian heritage using a combination of cultural diplomacy, security surveillance, and strong legal action.

The ministry’s undersecretary, Qasim al-Sudani, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the government’s agenda prioritizes the tourism sector.

The strategy emphasizes recovering documented items that were assigned official museum inventory numbers prior to their theft and smuggling, especially during the tumultuous period following the 2003 US-led invasion.

The initiative also seeks to tackle the significant number of unrecorded artifacts found during illegal and random excavations.

Since these items lack formal records, they pose a substantially more difficult legal issue to monitor and authenticate.

The Iraqi government has formed a combined domestic task force comprising the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Interior, the National Intelligence Service, and the National Security Service to carry out the plan.

Security agencies are cooperating with Iraqi embassies to identify stolen treasures that appear at public or private auctions abroad.

While countries like the United Kingdom and the United States have actively assisted in the return of tens of thousands of artifacts, Iraqi officials have indicated that some nations have intentionally delayed the repatriation process.

Iraq is also taking legal actions internationally against foreign businesses or individuals who are keeping Iraqi artifacts.

World.title: Iraq evaluates exploration blocks to optimize gas output
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil is actively assessing its exploration blocks and foreign alliances to maximize domestic gas output.

Director of the state-owned Midland Oil Company (MOC), Mohammed Yassin Hassan, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the ministry is focusing on unexploited exploration areas rather than existing resources.

The strategic measure seeks to attract multinational corporations to invest in Iraq’s growing natural gas sector.

Instead of altering production at current sites, the Oil Ministry is focusing on new exploration regions to identify new deposits.

Due to the strong interest in Iraq’s untapped energy potential, multinational energy businesses have already begun contacting the ministry.

Iraq’s MOC is actively pursuing partnerships with major US firms, such as ConocoPhillips, to lead gas development projects in important areas in the provinces of Diyala and Anbar.

Expanding operations in blocks such as the Akkas and Mansuriya gas fields is critical to Iraq’s long-term strategy for achieving energy independence and providing the necessary fuel for power plants to generate electricity.

World.title: Marsoumi: Iraq’s 10M bpd oil goal faces $75B cost and OPEC+ hurdles
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s strategic plan to scale crude oil production to 10 million barrels per day (bpd) by 2030 faces formidable structural, financial, and geopolitical hurdles, prominent Iraqi economic analyst Dr. Nabil Al-Marsoumi warned on Wednesday, September 2, 2026.

The assessment follows directives issued on Tuesday by Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi, who instructed the Ministry of Oil to expand exploration licensing rounds and ramp up extraction across fields in federal territory and the Kurdistan Region to target nearly 10 million bpd over the next four years.

Al-Marsoumi outlined four primary structural constraints standing between Iraq’s current production baseline and the 10-million-bpd horizon:

OPEC+ Baseline & Quota Negotiation: Iraq currently produces approximately 4.431 million bpd against an OPEC+ baseline allocation of 4.651 million bpd. Pushing production toward 10 million bpd requires formal revision of Iraq’s sovereign quota—a concession requiring consensus among major OPEC+ members.

Sustainable Capacity Ceiling: US petroleum consultancy DeGolyer and MacNaughton is actively auditing the maximum sustainable capacity across 19 OPEC+ nations. Preliminary assessments project Iraq’s sustainable 12-month ceiling at 5.0 to 5.5 million bpd, revealing a 4.5-million-bpd capacity deficit below the 2030 target.

Capital Expenditure Threshold ($75 Billion): Based on global industry benchmarks averaging $15 billion in capital investment per 1 million bpd of added capacity, Iraq must mobilize roughly $75 billion in upstream and midstream funding. This capital must finance seawater treatment and injection facilities, storage farm expansions, pumping stations, and new maritime and northern pipeline export corridors.

Price Collapse & Market Saturation Risks: Global oil absorption capacity remains constrained by demand growth projections. Injecting millions of additional Iraqi barrels risks igniting a market-share price war among producers, which could trigger a global oil price collapse harmful to Baghdad’s hydrocarbon-dependent treasury.

Comparative Analysis: Current Capacity vs. 2030 Target

Metric / Parameter Current Level (2026) 2030 Government Target Gap / Required Expansion Crude Output ~4.431 Million bpd 10.000 Million bpd +5.569 Million bpd Sustainable Ceiling 5.0 – 5.5 Million bpd 10.000 Million bpd +4.500 Million bpd OPEC+ Production Baseline 4.651 Million bpd Revised Allocation Required Requires OPEC+ Consensus Estimated Capital Outlay Baseline operational budget ~$75 Billion cumulative $15B per 1M bpd capacity Export Infrastructure Constrained southern/northern routes New northern & deepwater sea lines Major pipeline & storage expansion

Al-Marsoumi cautioned that upstream expansion cannot occur in isolation from global energy market fundamentals. Without substantial foreign direct investment to finance water injection schemes and deepwater export berths, aggressive target-setting risks outpacing actual midstream logistics.

Furthermore, aggressively pursuing volume over price discipline could depress international crude benchmarks, reducing net state oil revenues even as export volumes increase.

World.title: IndiGo aircraft hits parking stand pole at Srinagar airport
World.content:
MUMBAI: An

aircraft operating from Navi Mumbai to Srinagar came into contact with a parking stand pole while parking at Srinagar International Airport on Friday, shortly after landing.

The aircraft departed Navi Mumbai at 6.50am and landed in Srinagar at 9.25am.

IndiGo, in a statement, said all passengers and crew were safe and had deplaned from the aircraft. The relevant authorities were immediately informed, and an investigation is underway. The aircraft has been grounded for necessary maintenance and will resume operations after securing the required clearances.

World.title: PM Modi congratulates 'friend' Meloni on becoming longest-serving postwar Italian PM
World.content:
Prime Minister

on Friday congratulated his Italian counterpart Giorgia Meloni, a day after she become Italy's longest continuously serving prime minister since the post- World War II era.

In a post on X, PM Modi said the milestone reflects Italian people's confidence in Meloni.

"Congratulations to my friend Prime Minister Meloni on becoming the longest continuously serving Prime Minister in Italy's postwar history. This milestone is a reflection of the trust and confidence of the Italian people in her leadership," the prime minister wrote.

"Her friendship has also been instrumental in advancing the India-Italy Special Strategic Partnership and I look forward to continuing our close cooperation to build a prosperous future for the people of our countries.

My best wishes for her continued success in the years ahead," he added.

The two leaders' widely known friendship is often referred to as "Melodi" - a combination of their surnames.

World.title: HarperCollins to publish Sonia Gandhi’s controversial memoir
World.content:
NEW DELHI: So, who does Sonia Gandhiâs controversial memoir âBelongingâ belong to? HarperCollins India has stepped in to publish the

leaderâs memoir, ending weeks of uncertainty over who would carry the domestic edition after Penguin Random House India (PRHI) exited the deal over some changes to the text.

The book will hit Indian shelves on November 10, 2026 â the same day as its international release.

Billed as one of the most anticipated political memoirs in recent years, Belonging is described as a personal account of love, identity, duty and belonging, offering an insider's perspective on India's political journey through Gandhi's own eyes.

Party leader Ashok Gehlot alleged that pressure had been exerted on Penguin to edit out sections dealing with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the RSS, and China's occupation of Indian territory during Modi's tenure, calling the episode a "murder of democracy.

World.content:
The final report will tell what caused the extremely rare instance of all three hydraulic systems on an A320 failing one after the other in a matter of seconds â whether it happened due to something going wrong with the hardware or software or due to some manual intervention.

NEW DELHI: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has made an âinterim safety recommendationâ the Directorate General of Civil Aviation urgently âtake appropriate actions as deemed fit to prevent abuse of psychoactive substanceâ in its preliminary report into the probe of the severe turbulence on Air Indiaâs Phuket-Delhi flight AI 2379 on Aug 4, 2026. While the probe is still on, the prelim report officially confirms that the âconfirmatory (dope) test report of the pilot-in-command (PIC) was found non-negativeâ and that the Airbus A320 had suffered an extremely rare multiple hydraulic failure.When the âeventâ occurred, âinitially, (the aircraft) gained 372 feet and fell by 292 feet from its assigned flight level of 36,000 feetâ¦. seat belt signs were off. Consequently, some passengers and cabin crew suffered injuries,â the report says. The âeventâsâ impact on the aircraft cabin damage was such that a âlavatory commode was uprooted from its original location.âThe report says in its conclusion: âDetailed investigation regarding technical and other aspects are underway. In this case, it has been observed that the PIC was found non-negative for psycho-active substance in the confirmatory test. The confirmation of use of psycho-active substances is a serious concern, and AAIB recommends appropriate actions by DGCA on priority.The preliminary report is published as per ICAO guidelines. The investigation is in progress. The final report will be published in due course.âThe final report will tell what caused the extremely rare instance of all three hydraulic systems on an A320 failing one after the other in a matter of seconds â whether it happened due to something going wrong with the hardware or software or due to some manual intervention.âAt 04:02:43 UTC, while cruising at flight level 36,000 feet, the aircraftâs flight control (F/CTL) system detected loss of green hydraulic system. Further, at 04:02:47 UTC, the flight control system detected loss of blue and yellow hydraulic systems. At 04:02:48 UTC, the autopilot got disengaged and a continuous repetitive chime (CRC) came. At 04:02:51 UTC, the Stall warning triggered for 2 seconds.ââThe co-pilot, who was the pilot flying (PF), responded and tried to control the prevailing situation. Subsequently, PIC took over the controls. Meanwhile, the aircraft encountered an altitude upset. Initially, it gained 372 feet and fell by 292 feet from its assigned flight level of 36,000 feet during the event. At around 04:02:52 UTC, the blue hydraulic system was recovered, and few seconds later, the yellow hydraulic and the green hydraulic systems were also recovered. Consequently, this led to the recovery of the flight control surfaces. Subsequently, the aircraft operation returned to its normal operating condition,â says the report.The hydraulics on an Airbus A320 use pressurised liquid to act as the "muscles" that move heavy flight controls, lower the landing gear, and stop the wheels. The hydraulics on an Airbus A320 use pressurised liquid to act as the âmusclesâ that move heavy flight controls, lower the landing gear, and stop the wheelsThe cabin supervisor (head cabin crew) apprised the cockpit about the injuries suffered by the passengers and cabin crew. The flight crew assessed the cabin situation and took the decision to continue the flight to its destination, Delhi and not divert to the nearest en route airport.The aircraft cabin suffered significant damage during the âeventâ. The overhead ceiling panel was found cracked or deformed at various places. Most of the passenger service unit (PSU) panels were found dislocated or bent at various places. The overhead handrail was found broken, and the sealing panel was found dislocated near the 10th row. The forward right-side emergency exit handle was found broken.In a statement, Air India said: âWe acknowledge the release of the preliminary report by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) and continue to extend our full cooperation to the investigation, including providing access to all relevant operational, maintenance and technical records. Safety remains Air India's highest priority. Our pilots undergo rigorous training, regular proficiency checks, medical examinations and other regulatory assessments in accordance with applicable national and international requirements.Following the incident, Air India has started voluntary testing of 100% of its pilots as a further step to reinforce its safety-first approach.ââThe airline maintains zero tolerance for any breach of safety, fitness or regulatory requirements and will take appropriate action wherever warranted. Air India remains committed to implementing any recommendations arising from the investigation,â AI said.

World.title: 'Will always face consequences': Yogi Adityanath warns 'anti-national' forces
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister

on Friday warned that anti-national and anti-social forces seeking to spread hatred or undermine India's unity would face consequences, invoking Lord Krishna's message on the occasion of Janmashtami.

Addressing a gathering in Mathura, the birthplace of Lord Krishna, on the second day of his visit, Adityanath emphasised that His teachings and message remained equally relevant today.

"Wherever the forces of goodness exist, they will be protected under all circumstances. But wherever anti-national and anti-social forces raise their heads, create hatred in society or attempt to harm India's unity, integrity and faith, Lord Krishna had already said 5,000 years ago what their fate would be," PTI quoted the chief minister as saying.

Yogi Adityanath also cited the Bhagavad Gita's teaching, "Paritranaya sadhunam, vinashaya cha dushkritam" (for the protection of the righteous and destruction of evil), stressing that it continued to guide society.

The chief minister highlighted the Braj region's role in preserving its religious heritage and the memories of Lord Krishna despite repeated invasions and attempts by various groups to impose their faith on India.

World.title: ‘Life in this vast metropolis has changed beyond recognition. Yet, I love Chennai just the way it is’
World.content:
I saw Madras for the first time in 1951, when I was 10 years old. It was a townish village. I was thrilled to travel in a tram. Buses were not very frequent. Pleasure, that was how a car was called, was rarely seen on the then narrow unmetalled roads. All roads were avenues lined with trees on either side.

In the house that I stayed in, the milkman would arrive by 6 a.m., along with a cow and its calf. Vendors selling vegetables, fruits, flowers, and curd would mark their attendance everyday without fail. We had pure drinking water, both from the wells and taps. Barely three years later, when I visited again, I noticed a few changes. No trams. More pleasure cars and buses. Yet, taxis were more popular.

From 1962, I became a permanent resident. My stay at a lodge on Pycrofts Road in Tiruvallikeni is still fresh in my memory. At Sydoji Mess, 30 meal tickets cost ₹10; ₹12 with curd. It was a small outlet capable of accommodating twelve persons at a time. We, the inmates of the lodge, would walk up to a nearby movie theatre for the second show and have ice cream at Buhari past midnight.

Those days are never to return. Life in this vast metropolis has changed beyond recognition. It is mechanical. Yet, I love Chennai just the way it is.

(As told to R. Srikanth)

World.title: Why should I make a U-turn?: Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar on parks amendment Bill
World.content:
Dismissing the claim that the government had been forced into a “U-turn” on the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Bill, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Friday (September 4, 2026) defended the withdrawal, saying the decision was taken to respect public sentiment and allow for a wider discussion on the legislation.

“Why should I make a U-turn? The sentiments of the people have been respected. We will release a list of what happened during the tenures of Yediyurappa and Bommai. There should be a discussion on this. There is no intention to build a tunnel through Lalbagh. Alternative routes will be examined,” Mr. Shivakumar, addressing the media here, said.

Flays BJP for being ‘anti-development’

The Bill, which sought to amend the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act, 1975, had drawn intense opposition from citizen groups and the opposition BJP over the provision allowing alienation of 5% of park land to be used for public infrastructure. The government withdrew it amid the controversy, with Mr. Shivakumar saying there was “nothing wrong in hearing their demands”.

Turning his attack on the BJP while speaking on concerns raised over tunnel road, Mr. Shivakumar accused the Opposition of being “anti-development” and questioned its record on major infrastructure projects in Bengaluru. “Even when Siddaramaiah had proposed a steel bridge earlier, the BJP opposed it. The BJP is anti-development. If Bengaluru has any curse, it is the BJP’s. Let them tell us if they started any major project of this kind during their tenure,” he said.

Mr. Shivakumar said tunnel roads, double-decker corridors and similar projects were necessary to address Bengaluru’s traffic congestion and “those who oppose tunnel roads should also say what their alternative is.”

He also questioned the BJP’s opposition to tunnel projects in Bengaluru, referring to projects in other States. “If that is the case, let the Opposition stop tunnel projects in Delhi and Maharashtra as well,” he said.

‘No intention of using Lalbagh land’

Mr. Shivakumar reiterated that the government had no intention of taking over Lalbagh land for the proposed 16.5-km tunnel road. “The Bill was withdrawn because we want to have a discussion. The government has no intention of taking over Lalbagh land for the tunnel road project. We are not selling parks. Land has to be transferred to provide space for the Metro,” he said, alleging that the Opposition had prevented a discussion on such issues in the Assembly. “We know that if we discuss important issues, their (opposition parties’) failures will come to light. That is why the Opposition did not allow the session to be held,” he said.

Defending the government’s handling of public land, he cited several instances in which land had earlier been provided for public infrastructure and institutions. “Public land had earlier been given for the Metro, High Court parking and in other cases. I have already said that we should all work together. If we accept suggestions, does that mean I have made a U-turn?” he argued.

On Lalbagh, he said the land under the Horticulture Department was being transferred and that special orders had been issued in the past for small parcels of land. “When officials proposed this, approval was given. It was not done specifically for the tunnel,” he maintained.

World.title: Bengaluru Minister Krishna Byre Gowda orders setting up of joint police-civic teams to monitor footpath encroachment
World.content:
Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda has directed officials to set up joint task forces comprising police and civic officials in each city corporation jurisdiction to prevent re-encroachment of footpaths cleared across Bengaluru.

The task forces will be responsible for sustained monitoring of cleared footpaths, jointly enforcing rules, and initiating action against repeat encroachers. The Minister issued the directions at a video conference meeting on September 3 to review footpath encroachments.

He has directed Commissioners of civic bodies to issue a joint order or circular institutionalising police-civic enforcement, defining the responsibilities and jurisdictions of officials, and establishing a system for swift action and regular review of re-encroachment cases.

Mr. Gowda said that the cleared footpaths should be subjected to regular as well as surprise inspections, with immediate action against fresh encroachments.

Marshals and beat police personnel have been directed to jointly conduct regular inspections. Cases of re-encroachment should be promptly identified, and reported with photographic and geo-tagged evidence, he said.

He called for stringent action against repeat violators, including registration of FIRs, seizure of materials used for encroachment, and higher penalties as per the rules.

Officials have also been directed to clearly identify roads where street vending is restricted or prohibited, and formally communicate the details to the police and civic authorities concerned. On major and high-traffic roads, measures should be taken to ensure that street vendors do not obstruct pedestrian or vehicular movement, he said.

Mr. Gowda directed officials to conduct a fresh, comprehensive survey of street vendors at the earliest. He instructed officials to complete pending statutory processes, including the constitution of Town Vending Committees, in accordance with the law.

World.title: UN rights chief calls for greater action to end Sri Lanka’s ‘long legacy of impunity‘
World.content:
Sri Lanka needs to do more to protect human rights, advance accountability, and end the “long legacy of impunity”, the United Nations Human Rights chief has said.

The Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights, in its latest report on Sri Lanka released on Thursday (September 3, 2026), said the government “has continued to denounce racism and promote national unity”, but “wider efforts to ensure truth and justice risk being stalled and the momentum for transformative change being lost”.

The report, released ahead of the 63rd session of the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva beginning next week, comes even as President Anura Kumara Dissanayake completes two years in office, after a historic mandate, including from the island nation’s ethnic minorities.

Examining his government’s pre-election pledges and commitments made during UN High Commissioner Volker Türk’s visit to Sri Lanka in June 2025, the report acknowledged the government’s “notable steps” to tackle corruption, high-profile arrests and police-led investigations into certain political killings, enforced disappearances, and the 2019 Easter Sunday attacks. However, it observed “meaningful progress” remains “largely absent” in relation to accountability for international crimes allegedly committed by both State security forces and the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam during the nearly three decade-long armed conflict.

Just ahead of his election in September 2024, Mr. Dissanayake told The Hindu in an interview that fixing Sri Lanka’s crisis-hit economy — the island defaulted on its debt in 2022 — and wiping out racism would be “top priorities” for his National People’s Power (NPP) government. Opting to continue with an ongoing International Monetary Fund programme, which imposed crushing austerity measures, President Dissanayake’s government has maintained that economic recovery would remain its priority.

Meanwhile, as the UN report noted, successive external shocks, including unilateral trade measures, the devastating Cyclone Ditwah of 2025, and spillovers from conflicts in West Asia, have further affected the local economy and people’s living standards.

Recalling the NPP’s election promise to introduce a new constitution that ‘guarantees equality, democracy and the devolution of political and administrative power to every local Government, district and province’, the report pointed to the Provincial Council elections that are pending for over a decade.

Further, the report highlighted the NPP’s pledge to repeal the draconian Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA) and urged the government to impose a moratorium on the legislation, expedite its repeal, and ensure that any replacement legislation complies with international human rights law. “The Government continued to apply the PTA, resulting in arbitrary arrests and prolonged detentions without charge,” it said, adding that the High Commissioner’s office received information from Sri Lanka’s Human Rights Commission on 46 PTA-related detention cases in 2025 and 12 cases as of March 2026.

‘Mixed results’

A recent report published by global rights monitor Human Rights Watch points to Sri Lanka’s “lack of will” to prosecute past abuses. It highlighted the Chemmani mass grave site near Jaffna, where more than 580 skeletons have been unearthed so far, as families of Tamils killed or disappeared during the war wait to see how the government might proceed with the findings at the country’s largest mass grave.

Also read: A poverty of hope among Sri Lankan Tamils

Authored by Sri Lankan human rights activist and lawyer Bhavani Fonseka, the report said the Dissanayake administration had provided “an opening” to address the Chemmani mass grave and some other serious international crimes, including the 2019 Easter Sunday bombings, but that “results to date are mixed.” Based on interviews with victims, families of disappeared persons, activists and lawyers, it said: “The administration’s encouraging actions are only first steps, and significant barriers to genuine accountability remain.”

World.title: CBI searches 89 locations across 20 States in crackdown against “digital arrest” syndicates; 3 held
World.content:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has carried out searches at 89 locations across 20 States in connection with three major “digital arrest” scam cases as part of Operation Chakra-VI, arresting three persons so far.

The coordinated searches were aimed at tracing the proceeds of fraud and identifying the beneficiaries and handlers behind the syndicates, the agency said on Friday (September 4, 2026).

“The operations were meticulously planned on the basis of detailed financial and technical analysis, including examination of bank accounts and online account access data,” it said.

One of the cases pertains to BITS Pilani, where the victim was kept under “digital arrest” for three months, and ₹7.67 crore was extorted from him by scammers posing as police officers.

In another case, the accused used a similar modus operandi to trap a resident of Gujarat into believing that he had been digitally arrested. The victim was kept under “digital arrest” for three months and allegedly extorted of ₹19.24 crore.

In the third case, a victim in Karnataka was forced to pay ₹15.45 crore over a period of one month.

“The searches led to the seizure of incriminating banking documents, account-related records, digital devices, and other crucial evidence, which are now being forensically examined to unravel the wider financial and technological infrastructure sustaining the "digital arrest" syndicates operating across State boundaries,” the agency said.

Three arrested

During the operation, the CBI arrested three persons. Their examination revealed their specific roles in receiving, layering and dispersing the fraud proceeds, the investigating agency said.

“Akash, a resident of Haryana, was found to have received ₹1.95 crore of the defrauded amount into his account. He had opened the account himself and swiftly transferred the money to other accounts on the same day, establishing his direct link to laundering the proceeds,” the CBI said.

The agency said accused Raja Karmakar of Kolkata received ₹1.5 crore of the fraud proceeds in his firm’s account. It alleged that Jyoti Rani, into whose account a portion of the defrauded sum was credited, withdrew part of it in cash and transferred the remaining amount to other accounts, thereby actively participating in dispersing the money to obscure its trail.

“Efforts are underway to track down and apprehend the remaining accused involved in the wider network,” the CBI said.

Taking serious note of the alarming scale of such crimes, the Supreme Court has directed the CBI to take concerted action against the perpetrators and the wider networks facilitating such offences.

World.title: What did the Supreme Court say about paid maternity leave?
World.content:
The story so far: Last week, the Supreme Court ruled that adoptive mothers could avail themselves of 12 weeks of paid maternity leave regardless of the age of their children at the time of adoption. Striking down Section 60(4) of the Social Security Code, 2020 (previously Section 5(4) of the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961), which limited this benefit only to mothers who adopted children under the age of three months, the Court said that an adoptive mother had the same rights and obligations towards the child as a biological mother.

What is the law on maternity leave in India?

Statutory maternity benefits for working women in India began to be granted in colonial times. The Bombay Maternity Benefit Act, 1929, covered women factory workers. It was followed by similar laws in other parts of the country in the run-up to Independence. In 1961, Parliament passed the Maternity Benefit Act to provide paid maternity leave of 12 weeks to working women across the country.

In 2017, the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act not only extended the period of paid maternity leave for biological mothers to 26 weeks, but also inserted a provision extending maternity leave for the first time to adoptive mothers or surrogate mothers. Section 5(4) of the Act stated that surrogate or adoptive mothers legally adopting a child below three months would be entitled to maternity leave for a period of 12 weeks from the date the child is handed over to the mother.

Why was this law considered inadequate?

Also Read: What legal protections exist for women returning from maternity leave?

This provision was challenged in 2021 by Hamsaanandini Nanduri, a lawyer who adopted siblings in 2017. Ms. Nanduri told The Hindu that her Bengaluru-based law firm gave her only six weeks of paid maternity leave. “I could not leave my young children at home to turn up in office after just six weeks, so I took some additional months of unpaid leave. But it made me angry that there was no policy about it,” she said.

Terming the 12 weeks of maternity leave granted in 2017 to adoptive or surrogate mothers as “mere lip service”, the petitioner contended that when compared to the 26 weeks of maternity leave granted to biological mothers, the provision violated the fundamental rights guaranteed under the Constitution.

The three-month limit was unjust to both children and parents, depriving older adoptees from receiving the maternal care they need for their development and integration into their adoptive families, her lawyer argued.

The petitioner also pointed out in Court that adoption procedures take much longer than three months in India.

Also, as Ms. Nanduri told The Hindu: “I found on filing an RTI (Right to Information) application with CARA (Central Adoption Resource Authority) that less than 5% of children adopted at that time were under the age of three months.”

What did the Court say about motherhood?

The Court made it clear that motherhood cannot be seen through the “narrow lens of biology” alone. It referred to adoption as part of the “right to reproductive autonomy”. It noted that “the period of leave plays a crucial role in fostering [an] emotional bond between the mother and the child”. The Court added that stress hormone levels in children raised in orphanages are often higher than those in children brought up in a familial environment, which pointed to a greater need for paid maternal leave for older adoptees.

How will the judgment help adoptees and their parents?

Madhumitha Venkataraman started interviewing for jobs as a senior HR executive while waiting for an adoption referral, stipulating in every interview that she would need paid time off to support her child. Several multinational organisations balked at the idea of granting leave for more than a few weeks. But Ms. Venkataraman was finally recruited by a global media company that promised her one year of paid maternity leave. “My son came home at the age of three and a half months in 2023, so I was not eligible for maternity leave under the old law. But because this company was so accommodating, I did not have to choose between my career and my parenting,” she said. “There are emotional needs, and not just for the child. The time at home with my son gave me space to grow into motherhood,” she said. It is this time and space that other adoptive mothers say they will be entitled to as well, from now.

Noopur Goyal’s daughter was 15 months old when she came home in 2021. “I worked as a paediatric cardiologist at a top hospital in Delhi. I knew there was no provision for maternity leave, so I had to give up my job,” said Dr. Goyal, a single parent who works as a freelance consultant in Noida. “I had brought her into a new world, so I had to be present for her. An adopted child has been uprooted twice. I needed the time at home with her to build attachment and give her a sense of security.” Dr. Goyal said she was financially stable to be able to do this, but she is “glad now that there is a law mandating 12 weeks of paid maternity leave for all adoptive mothers.”

What did the Court say about paternity leave?

The Court also called on the Union government to examine the need for a formal law recognising paternity leave for all fathers, adoptive or biological. Noting that India’s legal framework does not adequately account for the role of fathers in childcare, it underlined the importance of shared parenting. As of now, only male government servants are entitled to 15 days’ paternity leave for the birth of a child or adoption. Leaves in the private sector are generally determined by company policies.

World.title: Delhi HC issues notice on plea seeking policy for women athletes returning after maternity
World.content:
The Delhi High Court on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) sought the response of the Centre, the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) and the Indian Olympic Association on a petition by wrestler Vinesh Phogat, seeking a structured framework to facilitate the return of women athletes to competitive sports after pregnancy and maternity leave.

Also Read: What legal protections exist for women returning from maternity leave?

Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma issued the notice on the plea and listed the matter for further hearing on November 18.

Senior advocate Rajshekhar Rao, appearing for Ms. Phogat, said: “This is a larger question on lady athletes and maternity leave and impact on their ability to participate in the sport”. Mr. Rao pointed out that international standards provide certain benefits and protection of rankings to athletes who take maternity leave.

In the plea, Ms. Phogat sought directions for the formulation of a fair and structured framework for women athletes returning from maternity, transparent and objectively verifiable selection and nomination processes, as well as an alternative mechanism for athletes disadvantaged by maternity-related absences.

Ms. Phogat, who gave birth to a child in July 2025, has contended that after resuming her wrestling career, she was required to re-enter the competitive pathway without any accommodations for the period during which she could not compete due to maternity.

According to the plea, the eligibility criteria relied on performances in tournaments held during her maternity period, effectively penalising her for an absence over which she had no control, instead of providing an alternative route for her return to competition.

Challenges WFI notice

Ms. Phogat has also challenged two show-cause notices issued by the WFI and the disciplinary proceedings initiated against her.

The court asked the WFI’s counsel to obtain instructions on the matter and listed the challenge to the notices for hearing on September 29.

WFI’s counsel submitted that the federation had given Ms. Phogat two opportunities for a hearing but there had been “no show”. A final opportunity had now been granted and the hearing was scheduled for September 2, the counsel said.

World.title: Heated exchange in T.N. Assembly as Udhayanidhi Stalin questions CM Vijay’s government on law and order
World.content:
A heated exchange erupted in the Tamil Nadu Assembly on Thursday (September 3, 2026) when the Leader of Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin charged that law and order situation has deteriorated since the TVK-led government assumed office in May this year.

Initiating the debate on demand for grants for the Police and Fire and Rescue Departments, headed by Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay, the DMK leader claimed no action was taken against TVK functionaries involved in criminal cases. A visibly upset, Minister for Rural Development and Water Resources N.Anand, intervened and countered the allegation by reading out the action against his party functionaries. Immediately, the DMK MLAs stood on their feet and said the Leader of Opposition should not be interrupted while making his speech. Minister Aadhav Arjuna, Raj Mohan and C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar also made interventions, leading to strong opposition from DMK legislators.

Resuming his speech Mr. Udhayanidhi said, “Around 550 criminal incidents have been reported in the past 116 days, including 200 murders; more than 300 cases of sexual assault; eight custodial deaths; and 10 ‘honour’ killings. The ruling party says the government has not even completed six months in office. That argument may apply to the implementation of its electoral promises...I do not dispute it. However, it cannot be used as an excuse when it comes to the law-and-order situation.”

Mr. Udhayanidhi said the ruling TVK government in 116 days of power, instead of introducing new schemes, has cancelled several projects launched by the previous DMK regime. “The government either announces a change of name or declares that a scheme has been scrapped,” he pointed out.

According to Mr. Udhayanidhi aid when the DMK was in power, Tamil Nadu was moving in top gear. But in these 116 days, Tamil Nadu is now moving in reverse gear, he alleged. “The functioning of this government appears to be focused more on ensuring that the reels posted by it [on social media] reach the public than on ensuring that its schemes reach the intended beneficiaries,” he charged.

Stating that the Fifth Police Commission had given nearly 800 recommendations in total and out of those, 86 recommendations were progressively implemented during the DMK administration, he urged the government to implement the remaining long-term recommendations in phases.

The House continued to witness heated exchange between MLAs of the two parties for nearly two hours.

‘Run away’ remarks: CM Vijay vs. Udhayanidhi

Around 1.15 pm, Chief Minister Mr. Vijay rose and remarked, “I shall answer all questions [on Monday next] but the Opposition should promise that they won’t run away.” With those remarks, Mr. Vijay left the Assembly.

Later Mr. Udhayanidhi retorted that the Chief Minister himself “ran away” from the Assembly.

World.title: 12 terrorists killed in intelligence-based operation in Balochistan's Kalat: ISPR
World.content:
Security forces killed 12 terrorists in an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Balochistan’s Kalat district, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Friday.

The IBO was conducted on Wednesday on the reported presence of terrorists belonging to the Indian proxy Fitna al Hindustan, the military’s media wing said in a press release.

The state has designated Balochistan-based terrorist groups as Fitna al Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

“During the conduct of the operation, the terrorists’ hideout was identified, monitored and busted through prompt surgical action,” it said, adding that “all 12 Indian-sponsored terrorists” were killed.

A cache of ammunitions and improvised explosive devices were also destroyed on-site, it added.

It said that sanitisation operations were being conducted to eliminate any other Indian-sponsored terrorist found in the area.

It added that a relentless counter-terrorism campaign under “Azm-i-Istehkam” by security forces and law enforcement agencies would “continue at full pace to wipe out menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country”.

President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif paid tribute to the security forces for eliminating the dozen terrorists in Kalat.

In separate statements carried by state-run APP, the president and the prime minister expressed their resolve to completely eradicate the menace of terrorism from the country.

They said the entire nation stood firmly with the armed forces in their unwavering resolve to safeguard the country.

“The continuous operations by law enforcement agencies and security forces are aimed at completely eliminating terrorism being patronised by external elements,” President Zardari was quoted as saying.

PM Shehbaz said the government will never allow terrorists to succeed in their nefarious designs to disrupt peace in Balochistan.

5 injured as coordinated attack in Bhag foiled

Separately, two policemen were among five people injured as law enforcers foiled a “coordinated” terrorist attack on a police station, bank and the office of the assistant commissioner in Balochistan’s Bhag city, the provincial government said on Friday.

Shahid Rind, the chief minister’s aide for political and media affairs, said in a post on X that about 40 terrorists attacked the three places using “heavy weapons, rocket launchers, machine guns, sniper rifles and hand grenades”.

Rind said the terrorists failed to take control of the Bhag police station or seize weapons from the facility.

He highlighted that the cops “bravely confronted the terrorists for nearly two hours”, inflicting heavy casualties and material loss to the attackers, who were “forced to retreat”. The CM’s aide noted that the strong protective wall of the police station played a crucial role in the defensive action.

Rind further said that the terrorists failed to loot cash from the “national bank”, while a special branch of the Bomb Disposal Unit defused an improvised explosive device (IED) planted by the terrorists in the facility.

Two police personnel were injured by the terrorists’ firing, while three citizens were also hurt, Rind said, adding that medical aid was being provided to them all.

Following the terrorist attack, the people of Bhag expressed solidarity with police and lauded their bravery, he said, affirming that the people of Balochistan stood with police and security forces in the fight against terrorism.

“Bhag police proved that terrorists would not be allowed to challenge the writ of the state,” Rind asserted.

Surge in terrorism

The Kalat IBO and the Bagh attack come amid a recent surge in terrorist activities in Balochistan.

On the night of Aug 31-Sept 1, Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) terrorists launched a coordinated attack on the Customs House, located at Ziarat Cross on the N-50 National Highway, in Pishin district.

While security forces responded effectively and killed 10 terrorists, two officers were among six martyred in the fire exchange, ISPR said.

Also on August 31, 11 terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan, who had blocked the N-40 Quetta-Taftan highway by establishing an illegal checkpoint for extortion in Chagai’s Nokcha area, were eliminated following an intense exchange of fire.

According to security officials, a convoy of “empty vehicles” from the Reko Diq copper and gold project had come under attack in the same area of Nokcha while it was travelling to Quetta from the project site.

The same day, it was reported that two terrorists had also been killed during an IBO in Washuk district.

Last month, the security situation remained most severe in Balochistan, where the number of terrorist attacks increased by seven per cent from 83 in July to 89 in August, according to a monthly assessment by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS).

World.title: PM Shehbaz discusses need for ML-1 railway project's early groundbreaking in meeting with ADB official
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif discussed the need for Karachi-Peshawar Main Railway Line’s (ML-1) early groundbreaking with Asian Development Bank (ADB) South, Central, and West Asia Vice President Yingming Yang on Friday.

The premier and the visiting ADB official held a meeting in Islamabad, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said in a statement, adding that a central focus of the discussion was the modernisation of ML-1.

The long-delayed project was a “vital national infrastructure priority”, the statement said.

During the meeting, PM Shehbaz stressed that upgrading the project was essential for modernising freight logistics, strengthening regional trade connectivity and supporting major industrial initiatives, it said.

Moreover, the “meeting discussed the need for the early groundbreaking of ML-1, being vital for infrastructure development and modernising the connectivity”, it added.

The $10 billion ML-1 project is among the public-private partnership initiatives for which Pakistan is seeking ADB’s scaled-up financing.

Pakistan has already secured $2bn in financing from the Manila-based lending agency for the Karachi-Rohri section of the 1670-km ML-1 project, which is under implementation.

In July, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal told the media that the groundbreaking of the first phase of the project, part of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), was to take place early next year.

Asked if the ADB loan for the project was acquired after China declined to take up the scheme, as it used to be the preferred financier under the CPEC, the minister did not agree, saying all three modes, including local, Chinese and multilateral financing, were part of the plan under the CPEC framework agreement for ML-1. “It was agreed with China under the CPEC framework that ML-1 would be financed jointly through Chinese, Pakistani and multilateral sources,” he said.

However, given the ongoing annual rollovers of existing Chinese loans, it was considered prudent to start the project with ADB financing in the initial phase, and it was done with China’s consent.

Previously, Pakistan had been requesting the Chinese side to depute technical teams for technical and financial terms and conditions for well over two years after the project size was scaled back for cost-cutting.

Country Partnership Strategy discussed

In Friday’s meeting, PM Shehbaz also lauded ADB’s “consistent professionalism and responsiveness in delivering transformative urban infrastructure, transport, and public service projects in Pakistan”, the PMO statement said.

It added that he and Yang also reviewed the multi-decade development partnership and charted priority interventions under the new Country Partnership Strategy (CPS) 2026–2030, the PMO statement said.

Yang is leading an ADB delegation, which is in Islamabad as part of a follow-up to the $10bn CPS, approved in March this year.

In March, ADB announced the five-year CPS, under which it would extend about $10 billion in financing to Pakistan.

The CPS sets out “a roadmap to support the country’s transition to sustainable and inclusive growth through private sector-led development”, the Manila-based lending agency said at the time.

PM Shehbaz told the ADB official that Pakistan has “successfully navigated a difficult economic turnaround through rigorous fiscal, structural, and governance reforms”.

These corrective actions had restored macroeconomic stability, reinforced investor confidence and earned stable outlook upgrades from major international credit rating agencies including Fitch, Moody’s, and S&P, he said.

Reaffirming his government’s “steadfast commitment to long-term economic transformation”, the PM said administrative bottlenecks were being actively dismantled through dedicated execution task forces, the PMO statement said.

It added that the two also discussed expanding cooperation in different sectors, exploring “collaborative avenues in support of the private sector, energy security, food security, export competitiveness, artificial intelligence and information technology”.

“The meeting concluded with a mutual pledge to translate the strategic priorities of the CPS 2026–2030 into concrete, high-impact results that drive sustainable growth and visibly enhance the standard of living for the people of Pakistan,” the statement said.

The PM also welcomed Yang on his first official visit to Pakistan as the ADB vice president for South, Central, and West Asia.

World.title: Scuffle in Karachi's DHA: Inquiry report says allegations in FIR 'not substantiated'
World.content:
KARACHI: An inquiry report into a scuffle at an apartment building in Defence Housing Authority’s (DHA) Phase 6, CCTV footage of which went viral on social media, said that the allegations in the first information report (FIR) were “not substantiated” by the findings while also recommending departmental action against police officials involved in the incident, it emerged on Friday.

Last week, CCTV footage of the physical altercation between the residents of an apartment building in DHA’s Phase 6 surfaced on social media. The footage showed police officials restraining a woman as she was attacked by another woman with a dumbbell.

However, the FIR of the incident was registered against the woman who was assaulted and her brother. Subsequently, an inquiry was ordered into the incident.

The inquiry report was submitted to the Karachi police additional inspector general by South Deputy Inspector General (DIG) South Zone Syed Asad Raza.

The report said that a fact-finding enquiry was conducted to ascertain the actual turn of events, determine the circumstances leading to the altercation, and examine the conduct of police officials present at the scene.

It said that all available documentary and electronic data and departmental records were scrutinised, while CCTV footage and mobile phone footage was also examined. It further said that the statements of 13 people were also recorded.

The report found that the incident was sparked by a parking dispute between the mother-in-law of Korangi Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Fida Hussain Janwari and another resident.

It identified the police officials visible in the CCTV footage as constables Saqib and Haider Sultan. It further added that the plainclothes man who destroyed the CCTV camera in the footage was Constable Taimoor Ahmed, while the official who handed over his weapon for this purpose was Constable Amir Sohail.

“All were detailed for duty at the private bungalow of the Korangi SSP,” it said.

In its recommendations, the report said that the allegations registered in the FIR did not “substantiate” the findings, and directed that the case be disposed off in accordance with the law.

It also said that an FIR should be registered against the SSP’s mother-in-law and her daughter and son as well as the police officials present at the time of the incident, while the “victim family shall be encouraged to initiate legal action at free will against them”.

It further said that the on-the-spot arrests in the case without justifiable evidence by Darakshan Station House Officer Rashid Ali and Assistant Sub-inspector Aftab Mangi were not justifiable and spoke of the officials’ “tilt towards the aggressive party”.

It said that the investigating officer, identified as SIP Imran, also undertook “no serious efforts” to collect evidence and did not independently apply his mind to investigate the case.

“Hence, all three officials of District South are recommended to be strictly proceeded against departmentally for miscarriage of justice,” it said.

The report said that the actions of constables Taimoor and Amir, specifically the facilitating of one party in the fray to the detriment of the other and vandalising the CCTV camera, “far exceed the pale of lawful duty, bordering on criminal misconduct”.

It also said that constables Saqib and Haider, acting as “minions” of the perpetrators, “overlooked their basic duty as guardians of rights of people”.

“Their negligence and partisanship led to physical assault and further escalation. Had they merely intimated immediate senior or local police about the impending situation, the worse could have been averted. Strict departmental action is recommended against all four officials commensurate with their misconduct under the relevant rules,” it said.

It further said that the “lapse of supervision and lack of control over his subordinates is evident on the part of the Korangi SSP”. It called for examining his overall conduct in light of Civil Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 2020 and to take further action in this regard.

The inquiry report said that police officers must be strictly advised to train and supervise cops assigned for staff duties to act lawfully and treat fellow citizens fairly and respectfully in their daily interactions with the public.

“When faced with acrimonious situations, it is their bounden duty to act lawfully and bring such matters to the notice of their immediate senior instead of taking instructions from family members who are not authorised so that such violations are avoided in the future,” the report concluded.

CCTV and FIR

In the CCTV footage of the incident, a woman can be seen rushing down a flight of stairs with a dumbbell in her hand and charging at another woman before using it to hit her.

The video also showed two individuals in what appeared to be police uniforms restraining the woman being assaulted, and a man who came up the stairs shortly after and began arguing with the woman with the dumbbell.

At one point, the man and woman being assaulted managed to go inside what appeared to be their home, following which the woman with a dumbbell and another man began banging on their door and yelling obscenities.

At the end, a man in a shalwar kameez was seen using a weapon, provided by one of the people in uniform, to smash the CCTV camera.

But the incident’s first information report (FIR) offered a different version of events. It was registered at Darakhshan police station at 1:40am on Aug 21.

The FIR seen by Dawn invoked Sections 354 (assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty), 504 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of the peace), 506 (criminal intimidation), 337A(i) (punishment of shajjah), 382 (theft after preparation made for causing death, hurt or restraint to commit theft) and 34 of the Pakistan Penal Code.

In the FIR, the complainant described herself as a resident of the fourth floor of an apartment building, adding that a man, his sister and their mother — who resided on the third floor — came to their door and started kicking it.

The complainant alleged that the three family members hurled verbal abuses over a parking issue, and upon opening the door, began beating and threatening her.

Subsequently, local police arrived on the spot and took the brother and sister into custody, while their mother fled, the FIR said.

World.title: FO says Indian claims about Hindu temple in Narowal 'false, politically motivated'
World.content:
The Foreign Office (FO) on Friday rejected claims made by the Indian Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) regarding a Hindu temple in Narowal as “false and politically motivated”, adding that the neighbouring country was “distorting facts and resorting to cheap gimmicks”.

According to the government, the over-a-century-old temple in Siraj village had collapsed following torrential rains. A minority rights group, however, claimed that the structure was deliberately razed to facilitate the expansion of an adjoining seminary.

Subsequently, the Indian MEA issued a statement calling on the government to conduct a prompt and transparent investigation, condemning what it called a “reprehensible act of vandalism”.

In a statement shared on the social media platform X, FO Spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said Pakistan categorically rejected “the false and politically motivated assertions” made by India regarding the temple in Narowal.

He said, unlike the “false propaganda” being peddled by India, the temple’s structure was damaged on July 21 due to torrential rains.

“The local authorities have already surveyed the rain damage and initiated steps for the restoration of the building,” the spokesperson said.

“It is, therefore, shameful that India is distorting facts and resorting to cheap gimmicks,” he added.

The FO spokesperson said the “deliberate distortion of facts” could not distract attention from India’s “abysmal record of systematic persecution of minorities and state-sponsored attacks against their places of worship”.

“The world is well aware of the weaponisation of Hindutva ideology against minorities, and must hold the Indian leadership accountable for the persecution of Muslim, Sikh and Christian communities,” the FO spokesperson concluded.

World.title: 81 dead in Yemen clashes as Houthis push towards key strait: sources
World.content:
Clashes between Yemen’s Houthis and government forces have killed 81, military and medical sources said on Friday, as the rebels push towards territory bordering a chokepoint in the strategic Red Sea.

Fighting erupted on Thursday, after the Houthis launched a ground assault along with rocket and drone attacks near coastal areas, vying for control of the narrow Bab al-Mandeb strait at the Red Sea’s southern entrance.

The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi ships in recent weeks in the Red Sea, which has emerged as an alternative route for oil exports after Iran all but halted shipments from the Gulf by blockading the Strait of Hormuz.

The rebels are now trying to cement their hold over one of the world’s busiest shipping lanes, which they have disrupted with attacks on passing vessels since the Gaza war broke out in 2023.

The Houthi offensive aims to cut off the government-held port city of Mokha, under fire for weeks, and advance towards areas bordering the Bab al-Mandeb, military sources told AFP.

The rebels have seized elevated sites overlooking government positions near the Red Sea, the coastal town of Khokha and Taiz city further inland, a military source and a Taiz official told AFP, requesting anonymity.

The Houthis could target ships from these elevated positions, they said.

A military official on the coast said 24 of his men had been killed, while another in the Taiz area said 15 had died there. At least 42 Houthi fighters were also killed, according to medical sources in areas under their control.

Reinforcements sent

The Houthis want to control the hills overlooking Bab al-Mandeb and Mokha before attacking the coast, a Yemeni official in Aden, the government’s base since it was ousted from the rebel-held capital, Sanaa, in 2014.

The government has sent reinforcements to Taiz from Aden, the official said.

With Iran’s closure of Hormuz, the Bab al-Mandeb chokepoint has gained increased importance as a transit route for oil from Saudi Arabia, the world’s biggest exporter of crude.

The narrow waterway connects the Red Sea — and, via the Suez Canal, the Mediterranean — to the Indian Ocean.

A map showing the locations of the Bab al-Mandeb strait, Strait of Hormuz and Suez Canal. — made using ArcGIS/File

Although the Houthis do not control areas bordering Bab al-Mandeb, they hold the key port city of Hodeida north of Mokha.

In July, a fragile truce between the Houthis and the government fell apart after the rebels welcomed an Iranian plane to Sanaa, setting off a spate of attacks.

They later announced a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and began hitting its ships and territory as Yemen, following more than a decade of civil conflict, became the latest country drawn into the Middle East war.

World.title: Karachi court acquits driver in drug case filed over 2024 accident that killed 2 in Karsaz
World.content:
A Karachi court on Friday acquitted Natasha Danish, who was involved in the August 2024 Karsaz road accident, in a drug case against her, citing lack of evidence.

On Aug 19, 2024, a speeding Toyota Land Cruiser, driven by Danish, hit three motorcycles and another car on Karsaz Road, killing 60-year-old Imran Arif and his 22-year-old daughter Amna, as well as wounding three others.

The driver was arrested and booked on murder charges. Later, another case was lodged against her after medical reports confirmed that she was under the influence of methamphetamine (ice) at the time of driving.

In October 2024, Danish was acquitted in the murder case after a “compromise” pact between the parties.

On Friday, the judicial magistrate (East) heard the drug case against her, with Fawad Ali Khichi appearing as her counsel.

The court said the prosecution failed to prove the charges against the suspect.

Speaking to the media, Khichi said no traces of the narcotic methamphetamine (crystal meth) were found in Danish’s chemical examinations and blood tests.

He alleged that the police had tampered with the samples taken from Danish, adding that the investigating officer in the case had “hidden the blood test report”.

The case was registered under Section 11 (drinking liable to tazir) of the Prohibition (Enforcement of Hadd) Order (PEHO) of 1979 .

In May 2025, a judicial magistrate had dismissed Danish’s acquittal plea in the drug case.

Murder, drug cases in Karsaz accident

Danish was arrested on the spot and booked on murder charges after the Karsaz Road accident, which killed the father and daughter duo.

Later, Sindh Inspector General (IG) of Police Ghulam Nabi Memon said Danish’s medical report — conducted upon the request of the victims’ counsel — showed she was under the influence of crystal meth while driving.

Consequently, the police registered a separate first information report (FIR) against the driver under Section 11 (drinking liable to tazir) of PEHO 1979 .

On Sept 6, 2024, a sessions court had granted the suspect bail in the murder case after the victims’ family pardoned them “without any blood money”.

However, the same month, a judicial magistrate and a sessions court had separately rejected Danish’s bail pleas in the drug case.

Judicial Magistrate (East) Muhammad Raza Ansari had observed that her lawyer’s claim of the suspect’s blood and urine samples being manipulated was false. In the sessions court, state prosecutor Syed Khursheed Abbas Bukhari had opposed the bail application, arguing that the final charge sheet had yet to be submitted to the court.

Subsequently, through her lawyer, Danish had approached the SHC, where Justice Muhammad Karim Khan Agha approved her bail in the drug case after hearing arguments from both sides.

Two days before the SHC hearing, the Karachi police had filed a charge sheet against Danish before a judicial magistrate in the same case.

On Oct 31, 2024, a district and sessions court acquitted Danish in the murder case, with her lawyer saying that the court had “accepted the compromise application”.

World.title: Ex-Pakistan coach Jason Gillespie tells Aaqib Javed to 'look in the mirror' over cricket team sackings
World.content:
Former Pakistan Test coach Jason Gillespie said on Friday chairman of selectors Aaqib Javed needs to “look at himself in the mirror” with the national team “playing with fear”.

In a shock move Pakistan this week replaced head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and pace-bowling chief Umar Gul, and sent seven players home from England, in a dramatic response to successive Test thrashings.

Australia’s Gillespie, who led the side for eight months in 2024, including a 2-1 Test series win against England, said it was sad to see.

“I feel for the players, this is these guys’ livelihoods,” he told The Australian newspaper.*

“From the outside it looks like they are playing with fear.

“Salman Ali Agha goes from captaining the team in the first Test against England to out of the team for the second Test and on the plane home before the third Test,” he said.

“How does that work?” he asked, laying the blame firmly at the door of Javed.

“It’s pretty clear they don’t have a selection strategy at all, particularly under Javed. They change their mind like they change their pants — daily,” he said.

“Javed came out recently and blamed (former white-ball coach) Gary Kirsten and myself for everything that is going on.

“Javed has been chairman of selectors for the past two years. We haven’t even been there,” he said.

“Somehow he claims it is our fault. Make sense out of that. I think Javed needs to look at himself in the mirror,” he added.

The tourists suffered an innings and 103-run loss in the series opener at Headingley before going down by 194 runs at Lord’s.

The third and final Test starts at Edgbaston on September 9.

“There is definitely no communication between Javed, who is meant to be chairman of selectors, and the players,” added Gillespie.

“The players who were sacked heard it through family and friends and the media they had been sacked.

“How disrespectful is that?”

Several other ex-Pakistan coaches and players have been left similarly bewildered, including former captains Shahid Afridi and Shoaib Malik.

Ex-coach Mickey Arthur called it “an absolutely ridiculous situation”.

New Zealander Mike Hesson, who was already Pakistan’s white-ball chief, and Australian Ashley Noffke, have taken charge for the rest of the tour.

World.title: Anti-Narcotics Force says it helped US, Sri Lanka bust Afghanistan-based drug trafficking network
World.content:
The Anti-Narcotics Force (ANF) said on Friday that it had assisted in the busting of a transnational drug trafficking network through intelligence sharing.

The ANF said in a statement that it shared information with US and Sri Lankan authorities, who conducted an international joint operation, seizing 671 kilogrammes of methamphetamine (ICE) linked to the Afghanistan-based drug trafficking network from Karachi and Colombo ports.

On Wednesday, Sri Lankan police and the US embassy in Sri Lanka also announced the busting of a drug network and the seizing of almost half a tonne of crystal methamphetamine in a joint operation last month. However, they identified the drug network as Pakistani and said two Pakistani men had been arrested.

The US embassy in Colombo said the narcotics, valued at $21 million and concealed in bath towels, were meant to be smuggled to international markets via Sri Lanka.

In its statement, ANF said that, based on “actionable intelligence” provided by it, 200kg of methamphetamine was recovered from a container at Karachi Port. It said the mastermind of the network was also arrested, whom ANF identified as Ehsanullah, an Afghan.

Local handlers part of the network were also arrested, the statement added.

“After thorough investigations from the Afghan kingpin,” ANF said it shared “critical information” with Sri Lankan authorities and America’s Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA).

“This timely information resulted in recovery of 471kg of methamphetamine.”

The DEA then coordinated with Sri Lankan authorities and conducted a joint operation at Colombo Port, resulting in the recovery of 471kg of methamphetamine concealed in towels, ANF said.

According to ANF, the busted network was attempting to use Pakistani territory as a transit route for transporting narcotics to international destinations.

“Pakistan remains both a transit and victim state for Afghan-origin drugs,” ANF noted.

It said it utilised “advanced intelligence-based strategies” to identify the busted network”, adding that the “successful operation reflects ANF’s professional capabilities, commitment to combating narcotics trafficking, and its effective cooperation with international law enforcement agencies”.

“ANF’s efforts in dismantling international drug trafficking organisations and apprehending Afghan drug traffickers and their local facilitators have been formally acknowledged by Sri Lankan authorities and the US DEA, underscoring ANF’s effective role in international counter-narcotics cooperation,” the statement read.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
